title.zh: 卷三百四十二 列傳第一百〇一 梁燾 王巖叟 鄭雍 孫永
title.en: Volume 342 Biographies 101: Liang Dao, Wang Yansou, Zheng Yong, Sun Yong
title.raw: 卷三百四十二 列傳第一百〇一 梁燾 王巖叟 鄭雍 孫永 Volume 342 Biographies 101: Liang Dao, Wang Yansou, Zheng Yong, Sun Yong

sentences.zh: 梁燾 王岩叟 鄭雍 孫永

translations.literal: Liang Dao, Wang Yansou, Zheng Yong, Sun Yong
translations.idiomatic: Liang Dao, Wang Yansou, Zheng Yong, and Sun Yong

sentences.zh: 梁燾，字況之，鄆州須城人。

translations.literal: Liang Dao, courtesy name Kuangzhi, was a native of Xucheng in Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Dao, styled Kuangzhi, came from Xucheng in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 父蒨，兵部員外郎、直史館。

translations.literal: His father Qian was Vice Director in the Ministry of War and a direct appointee to the Historical Archives.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qian served as Vice Director of the Ministry of War and held a direct appointment in the Historical Archives.

sentences.zh: 燾以蒨任，為太廟齋郎。

translations.literal: Dao, through Qian's office, was made ritual officer of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's position, Dao received a yin privilege appointment as ritual officer at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 舉進士中第，編校秘閣書籍，遷集賢校理、通判明州，檢詳樞密五房文字。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, collated books in the Secret Repository, and was transferred to collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, vice commissioner of Ming Prefecture, and examiner of documents in the Five Bureaus of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, edited books in the Secret Repository, and was promoted to collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, vice commissioner of Mingzhou, and examiner of documents in the Five Bureaus of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 元豐時久旱，上書論時政曰：

translations.literal: During the Yuanfeng era, after prolonged drought, he submitted a memorial on current affairs, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanfeng period, when drought had long persisted, he submitted a memorial on affairs of state, saying:

sentences.zh: 陛下日者閔雨，靖惟政事之闕，惕然自責。

translations.literal: Your Majesty recently grieved over the lack of rain, calmly reflected on failings in government, and reproached yourself with vigilant remorse.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty recently lamented the drought, gave quiet thought to gaps in governance, and took yourself sternly to task.

sentences.zh: 丁卯發詔，癸酉而雨，是上天顧聽陛下之德言，而喜其有及民之意也。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao an edict was issued, and on the day guiyou rain fell—this shows Heaven heeding Your Majesty's virtuous words and rejoicing that you have the will to reach the people.
translations.idiomatic: An edict went out on dingmao day, and rain came on guiyou day—proof that Heaven heard Your Majesty's worthy words and was pleased by your intent to benefit the people.

sentences.zh: 當四方仰雨十月之久，民刻於新法，嗷嗷如焦，而京師尤甚，闤闠細民，罔不失職，智愚相視，日有大變之憂。

translations.literal: For ten months the realm had looked skyward for rain; the people were harried by the New Policies, crying out as if scorched—and the capital suffered most. Common folk in the market streets lost their livelihoods one and all; wise and simple alike looked at one another with daily dread of great upheaval.
translations.idiomatic: For ten months the land had prayed for rain while the people were ground down by the New Policies, wailing as though baked dry—and nowhere was the suffering worse than in the capital. Shopkeepers and humble townsfolk lost their means of living without exception; the learned and the simple stared at one another, day after day fearing catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 陛下既惠以詔旨，又施之行事，講除刻文，蠲損緡錢等，一日之間，歡聲四起。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has both shown kindness through edicts and carried it into action—revising harsh regulations, reducing tax levies in cash, and the like—so that within a single day cries of joy rose on every side.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has shown mercy in your proclamations and put that mercy into practice—easing oppressive rules, cutting back cash levies, and the like—so that in a single day shouts of rejoicing broke out everywhere.

sentences.zh: 距誕節三日而膏澤降，是天以雨壽陛下之萬年，感聖心於大寤，有以還其仁政也。

translations.literal: Three days before your birthday the nourishing rains descended—Heaven uses rain to bless Your Majesty with a reign of ten thousand years, moved by the great awakening of your sacred heart to restore benevolent government.
translations.idiomatic: Three days before your birthday the timely rains fell—Heaven sent rain to grant Your Majesty long life, stirred by the great awakening of your sacred heart and your return to humane rule.

sentences.zh: 然法令乖戾，為毒於民者，所變才能萬一。

translations.literal: Yet of the laws and ordinances that run contrary and poison the people, what has been changed amounts to perhaps one in ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yet among the statutes and regulations that violate justice and poison the people, perhaps one part in ten thousand has been altered.

sentences.zh: 人心之不解，故天意亦未釋，而雨不再施。

translations.literal: The people's hearts remain unsettled, and so Heaven's mind too has not been eased; rain has not come again.
translations.idiomatic: Because the people's hearts are still not at peace, Heaven's displeasure has not lifted either, and the rains have not returned.

sentences.zh: 陛下亦以此為戒，而夙夜慮之乎？

translations.literal: Does Your Majesty also take this as a warning and ponder it morning and night?
translations.idiomatic: Does Your Majesty take this as a warning and brood over it day and night?

sentences.zh: 今陛下之所知者，市易事耳。

translations.literal: What Your Majesty knows of now is merely the Market Exchange affair.
translations.idiomatic: What Your Majesty is aware of at present is only the Market Exchange policy.

sentences.zh: 法之為害，豈特此耶？

translations.literal: The harm the laws do—can it be limited to this alone?
translations.idiomatic: Can the damage wrought by these laws really be confined to that alone?

sentences.zh: 曰青苗錢也，助役錢也，方田也，保甲也，淤田也。

translations.literal: There are the Green Sprouts loans, the labour-exemption fees, equal-field measurement, the mutual-responsibility militia system, and silt-field reclamation.
translations.idiomatic: There are the Green Sprouts loans, the labour-exemption fees, equal-field surveys, the mutual-responsibility militia system, and silt-field reclamation.

sentences.zh: 兼是數者，而天下之民被其害。

translations.literal: All of these together have afflicted the people throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Taken together, these policies have brought suffering to the people across the empire.

sentences.zh: 青苗之錢未一及償，而責以免役；

translations.literal: Before Green Sprouts loans have even once been repaid, they are charged labour-exemption fees;
translations.idiomatic: Before Green Sprouts loans have even begun to be repaid, labour-exemption fees are already demanded;

sentences.zh: 免役之錢未暇入，而重以淤田；

translations.literal: before labour-exemption payments have even been collected, they are burdened again with silt-field levies;
translations.idiomatic: before labour-exemption payments have even been gathered in, silt-field levies are piled on top;

sentences.zh: 淤田方下，而復有方田；

translations.literal: silt-field orders have just been issued, and equal-field measurement follows again;
translations.idiomatic: silt-field orders have scarcely been issued when equal-field surveys follow again;

sentences.zh: 方田未息，而迫以保甲。

translations.literal: before equal-field work has subsided, they are pressed with the mutual-responsibility militia system.
translations.idiomatic: before equal-field work has even quieted down, the mutual-responsibility militia system is forced upon them.

sentences.zh: 是徒擾百姓，使不得少休於聖澤。

translations.literal: This only harasses the common people and keeps them from any brief respite in Your Majesty's gracious bounty.
translations.idiomatic: This does nothing but torment the common people and deny them even a moment's rest under Your Majesty's gracious rule.

sentences.zh: 其為害之實，雖一有言之者，必以下主吏，主吏妄報以無是，則從而信之，恬不復問，而反坐言者。

translations.literal: As for the actual harm they do—even when someone speaks of it, the inquiry is always delegated to local officials; the local officials falsely report that no such thing exists, and the court then believes them, calmly asks no further, and instead punishes the speaker.
translations.idiomatic: When anyone reports the harm these policies truly cause, the matter is always referred to the local magistrate; the magistrate falsely reports that nothing of the kind has occurred, the court accepts this without further inquiry, and the accuser is punished instead.

sentences.zh: 雖間遣使循行，而苟且寵祿，巧為妄誕，成就其事，至請遍行其法，上下相隱，習以成風。

translations.literal: Even when envoys are occasionally sent on inspection tours, they seek only to protect their salaries through perfunctory compliance, craftily fabricate reports, and help the policies succeed—even pleading to extend the laws everywhere—while superiors and subordinates conceal the truth from one another until it becomes ingrained custom.
translations.idiomatic: Even when inspectors are occasionally dispatched on circuit, they care only to safeguard their stipends, craftily invent false reports, and see the policies through—even urging that the laws be applied everywhere—while officials at every level cover for one another until concealment becomes the norm.

sentences.zh: 臣謂天下之患，不患禍亂之不可去，患朋黨蔽蒙之俗成，使上不得聞所當聞，故政日以敝，而禍亂卒至也。

translations.literal: I hold that the calamity of the realm lies not in the impossibility of removing disaster and rebellion, but in the formation of a custom of factional concealment, whereby those above cannot hear what they ought to hear—so that governance daily decays until disaster and rebellion arrive at last.
translations.idiomatic: I believe the empire's peril lies not in the difficulty of dispelling chaos and rebellion, but in the rise of a factional culture of concealment that keeps those above from hearing what they must hear—so that government grows more corrupt by the day until catastrophe finally arrives.

sentences.zh: 陛下可不深思其故乎？

translations.literal: Can Your Majesty not reflect deeply on the reason for this?
translations.idiomatic: Surely Your Majesty will give deep thought to why this is so?

sentences.zh: 疏入，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, but no response was issued.

sentences.zh: 內侍王中正將兵出疆，干賞不以法。

translations.literal: The eunuch Wang Zhongzheng led troops beyond the border and sought rewards without regard to regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The palace eunuch Wang Zhongzheng led troops across the frontier and demanded rewards in violation of the regulations.

sentences.zh: 燾爭之不得，請外，出知宣州。

translations.literal: Dao disputed this but could not prevail; he requested an outside post and was appointed prefect of Xuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dao contested the matter but could not prevail; he asked for an outside appointment and was sent out as prefect of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 入辭，神宗曰：「樞臣雲卿不肯安職，何也？」

translations.literal: On taking leave to depart, Emperor Shenzong said, "The chief minister says you refuse to rest easy in your post—why is that?"
translations.idiomatic: When he came to bid farewell, Emperor Shenzong said, "The chief minister tells me you are unwilling to remain at your post in peace—why is that?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣居官五年，非敢不安職，恐不勝任使，故去耳。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Your servant has held office for five years; it is not that I dare not rest easy in my post—I fear I am not equal to the commission, and that is why I leave."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I have served in office for five years. It is not that I refuse to stay at my post in peace—I fear I am not equal to the task, and that is why I am leaving."

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「王中正功賞文書，何為獨不可？」

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong said, "The documents for Wang Zhongzheng's merit rewards—why alone may they not pass?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong said, "The papers granting Wang Zhongzheng merit rewards—why alone may they not be approved?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「中正罔冒僥覬，臣不敢屈法以負陛下。」

translations.literal: He said, "Zhongzheng presumptuously seeks illicit gain; your servant dares not bend the law and fail Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Zhongzheng acts with reckless presumption and greedy ambition; I dare not distort the law and betray Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 未幾，提點京西刑獄，哲宗立，召為工部郎中，遷太常少卿、右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he was made fiscal commissioner of the judicial circuit of the western capital region. When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, he was summoned as Director in the Ministry of Works, then promoted to Vice Director of Ritual and Right Remonstrance Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed fiscal commissioner for the judicial circuit of the western capital region. When Emperor Zhezong took the throne, he was recalled as Director in the Ministry of Works, then promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Ritual and Right Remonstrance Councillor.

sentences.zh: 有請宣仁後御文德殿服袞冕受冊者，燾率同列諫，引薛奎諫章獻明肅皇后不當以王服見太廟事，宣仁後欣納。

translations.literal: When some proposed that Empress Dowager Xuanren should appear at Wende Hall in sacrificial robes and full regalia to receive investiture documents, Dao led his colleagues in remonstrance, citing Xue Kui's memorial that Empress Dowager Zhangxian-Mingsu should not appear before the Imperial Ancestral Temple in kingly dress; Empress Dowager Xuanren gladly accepted the advice.
translations.idiomatic: When others proposed that Empress Dowager Xuanren should receive investiture at Wende Hall dressed in sacrificial robes and full regalia, Dao led his colleagues in remonstrance, citing Xue Kui's argument that Empress Dowager Zhangxian-Mingsu ought not to appear before the Imperial Ancestral Temple in kingly garb; the Empress Dowager gladly accepted their counsel.

sentences.zh: 又論市易已廢，乞蠲中下戶逋負；

translations.literal: He also argued that since Market Exchange had been abolished, he petitioned to forgive overdue payments by middle and lower households;
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that since Market Exchange had been abolished, overdue debts owed by middle and lower households should be forgiven;

sentences.zh: 又乞欠青苗下戶，不得令保人備償。

translations.literal: he also petitioned that lower households indebted on Green Sprouts loans should not have guarantors made to cover repayment.
translations.idiomatic: and he also petitioned that lower households in arrears on Green Sprouts loans should not be forced to have guarantors make good the debt.

sentences.zh: 文彥博議遣劉奉世使夏國，御史張舜民論其不當遣，降通判虢州。

translations.literal: When Wen Yanbo proposed sending Liu Fengshi as envoy to Western Xia, Censor Zhang Shunmin argued he should not be sent and was demoted to vice commissioner of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Yanbo proposed dispatching Liu Fengshi as envoy to Western Xia, Censor Zhang Shunmin argued against the appointment and was demoted to vice commissioner of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 燾言：「御史持紀綱之官，得以犯顏正論，況臣下過失，安得畏忌不言哉？

translations.literal: Dao said, "The censor holds the office that maintains discipline and law; he may speak against the throne with a flushed face and set the record straight. When a subordinate is at fault, how can one hold back for fear and say nothing?
translations.idiomatic: Dao said, "The censor is the officer charged with upholding discipline; he is entitled to speak bluntly to the throne and set wrongs right. When a minister is at fault, how can one stay silent out of fear?

sentences.zh: 今御史敢言大臣者，天下之公議；

translations.literal: When a censor dares to speak against a great minister, that is the public judgment of the realm;
translations.idiomatic: When a censor dares to criticize a great minister, that voice belongs to the public judgment of the empire;

sentences.zh: 大臣不快御史者，一夫之私心。

translations.literal: when a great minister is displeased with a censor, that is the private resentment of a single man.
translations.idiomatic: when a great minister resents a censor, that is the private spite of one man.

sentences.zh: 罪天下敢言之公議，便一夫不快之私心，非公朝盛事也。」

translations.literal: To punish the public judgment of the realm for daring to speak, and to gratify the private resentment of a single man—this is no splendid affair for the court."
translations.idiomatic: To punish the empire's public voice for speaking out, and to indulge one man's private displeasure—this is no credit to the court."

sentences.zh: 時同論者傅堯俞、王岩叟、朱光庭、王覿、孫升、韓川，凡七人，悉召至都堂，敕諭以「事當權其輕重，故不惜一新進御史，以慰老臣。」

translations.literal: At this time seven who argued together—Fu Yaoyu, Wang Yansou, Zhu Guangting, Wang Di, Sun Sheng, and Han Chuan—were all summoned to the chief councillors' hall and instructed: "The matter must be weighed for relative gravity; therefore we do not regret sacrificing one newly appointed censor to comfort a senior minister."
translations.idiomatic: At the time, the seven who had spoken together—Fu Yaoyu, Wang Yansou, Zhu Guangting, Wang Di, Sun Sheng, and Han Chuan—were all summoned to the chief councillors' hall and told, "The matter must be weighed for its relative gravity; that is why we do not hesitate to sacrifice one newly appointed censor in order to placate a senior minister."

sentences.zh: 燾又言：「若論年齡爵祿，則老臣為重；

translations.literal: Dao also said, "If one judges by age, rank, and stipend, then the senior minister weighs heavier;
translations.idiomatic: Dao also said, "If one measures by age, rank, and emolument, the senior minister counts for more;

sentences.zh: 若論法度綱紀，則老臣為輕。

translations.literal: if one judges by law, institutions, and discipline, then the senior minister weighs lighter.
translations.idiomatic: but if one measures by law, institutions, and discipline, the senior minister counts for less.

sentences.zh: 御史者，天子之法官也，不可以大臣鞅鞅而斥去。

translations.literal: The censor is the emperor's judicial officer; he cannot be dismissed because a great minister is discontent.
translations.idiomatic: The censor is the Son of Heaven's officer of justice; he must not be driven out because a great minister is displeased.

sentences.zh: 願還舜民，以正國體。」

translations.literal: I ask that Shunmin be restored, to set right the dignity of the state."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Shunmin be restored to office, so that the proper dignity of the state may be upheld."

sentences.zh: 章十上，不聽。

translations.literal: He submitted ten memorials; the court would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted ten memorials in all; the court paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 燾又面責給事中張問不能駁還舜民制命，以為失職。

translations.literal: Dao also rebuked to his face Supervising Secretary Zhang Wen for failing to return and reject the edict concerning Shunmin, holding that he had neglected his duty.
translations.idiomatic: Dao also confronted Supervising Secretary Zhang Wen face to face, rebuking him for failing to return and reject the edict demoting Shunmin, which he regarded as a dereliction of duty.

sentences.zh: 坐詬同列，出為集賢殿修撰、知潞州，辭不拜，曰：「臣本論張舜民不當罷，如以為非，即應用此受斥。

translations.literal: For reviling his colleagues he was demoted to collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and prefect of Lu Prefecture; he declined the appointment, saying, "Your servant originally argued that Zhang Shunmin should not be dismissed. If I was wrong, I ought to be punished on that account.
translations.idiomatic: For insulting his colleagues he was demoted to collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and prefect of Luzhou; he refused to accept the appointment, saying, "I originally argued that Zhang Shunmin should not be removed. If I was in the wrong, I ought to be punished for that very reason.

sentences.zh: 今乃得以微罪冒美職，守劇郡，如此則朝廷命令，不能明辨曲直，以好惡示天下矣。」

translations.literal: Now I am allowed, on a trivial offense, to take a fine post and govern a difficult prefecture—if that is so, then the court's commands cannot clearly distinguish right from wrong and show the realm what is favored and what is not."
translations.idiomatic: Yet now, on a minor charge, I am offered a handsome post and a demanding prefecture—if that is how it stands, then the court's orders cannot clearly distinguish right from wrong or show the empire where favor and disfavor truly lie."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: No response was issued.

sentences.zh: 至潞，值歲飢，不待命發常平粟振民。

translations.literal: When he reached Lu, famine struck that year; without awaiting orders he opened the ever-normal granaries to relieve the people.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching Luzhou, he found famine that year; without waiting for authorization he opened the ever-normal granaries to feed the people.

sentences.zh: 流人聞之，來者不絕，燾處之有條，人不告病。

translations.literal: Exiles heard of this and came in an unbroken stream; Dao handled them in good order, and no one complained of hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees heard of this and came in an endless stream; Dao managed them with order and efficiency, and no one reported distress.

sentences.zh: 明年，以左諫議大夫召。

translations.literal: The following year he was recalled as Left Remonstrance Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled to serve as Left Remonstrance Councillor.

sentences.zh: 甫就道，民攀轅不得行，逾太行，抵河內乃已。

translations.literal: He had barely set out when the people clung to his carriage and would not let him go; they followed him over the Taihang Mountains until he reached Henei before they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He had scarcely begun his journey when the people seized the shafts of his carriage and would not let him leave; they escorted him over the Taihang range and did not turn back until he reached Henei.

sentences.zh: 既對，上書言：「帝富於春秋，未專宸斷；

translations.literal: After his audience he submitted a memorial saying, "The Emperor is rich in years but has not yet taken sole command of decisions;
translations.idiomatic: After his audience he submitted a memorial saying, "The Emperor is still young and has not yet assumed full personal authority;

sentences.zh: 太皇保佑聖主，制政簾帷，奸人易為欺蔽。

translations.literal: the Grand Empress Dowager protects the sacred sovereign and governs from behind the curtain, and wicked men easily deceive and conceal the truth.
translations.idiomatic: the Grand Empress Dowager protects the sacred sovereign and governs from behind the curtain, where unscrupulous men can easily mislead and deceive.

sentences.zh: 願正綱紀，明法度，採用忠言，講求仁術。」

translations.literal: I ask that discipline be set right, laws and institutions made clear, loyal counsel adopted, and humane governance pursued."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that discipline be restored, laws and institutions clarified, loyal counsel heeded, and humane governance pursued."

sentences.zh: 兩宮嘉納焉。

translations.literal: Both palaces praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Both palaces praised and accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 前宰相蔡確作詩怨謗，燾與劉安世交攻之。

translations.literal: The former chief councillor Cai Que wrote poems of resentment and slander; Dao joined Liu Anshi in pressing the attack against him.
translations.idiomatic: The former chief councillor Cai Que wrote poems full of resentment and slander; Dao joined Liu Anshi in pressing the case against him.

sentences.zh: 燾又言：「方今忠於確者，多於忠朝廷之士；

translations.literal: Dao also said, "At present those loyal to Que outnumber those loyal to the court;
translations.idiomatic: Dao also said, "Today those who are loyal to Que outnumber those loyal to the court;

sentences.zh: 敢為奸言者，多於敢正論之人。

translations.literal: those who dare speak wicked words outnumber those who dare speak upright words.
translations.idiomatic: and those who dare speak treacherous words outnumber those who dare speak honest ones;

sentences.zh: 以此見確之氣焰凶赫，根株牽連，賊化害政，為患滋大。」

translations.literal: From this one sees that Que's power and arrogance are fierce and overbearing, his roots and connections widespread; he corrupts customs, harms government, and the evil he brings grows ever greater."
translations.idiomatic: From this one can see that Que's influence is fierce and overbearing, his network of connections deep and wide; he corrupts public morals, poisons governance, and the harm he does grows ever greater."

sentences.zh: 確卒竄新州。

translations.literal: Que was finally banished to Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Que was ultimately exiled to Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 燾進御史中丞。

translations.literal: Dao was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Dao was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 鄧潤甫除吏部尚書，燾論潤甫柔佞不立，巧為進取。

translations.literal: When Deng Runfu was appointed Minister of Personnel, Dao argued that Runfu was soft, fawning, and unprincipled, and cunning in seeking advancement.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Runfu was appointed Minister of Personnel, Dao argued that Runfu was pliant, fawning, and without principle, and artful in pursuing advancement.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The court would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 改權戶部尚書，不拜，以龍圖閣直學士知鄭州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to acting Minister of Revenue; he declined the appointment and was made a direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to acting Minister of Revenue; he refused the appointment and was instead made a direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 旬日，入權禮部尚書，為翰林學士。

translations.literal: Ten days later he entered the capital as acting Minister of Rites and was made Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later he entered the capital as acting Minister of Rites and was appointed Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 元祐七年，拜尚書右丞，轉左丞。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanyou he was appointed Vice Director of the Right in the Secretariat, then transferred to Vice Director of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yuanyou he was appointed Vice Director of the Right in the Secretariat, then promoted to Vice Director of the Left.

sentences.zh: 蔡京帥蜀，燾曰：「元豐侍從，可用者多；

translations.literal: When Cai Jing was made military commissioner of Shu, Dao said, "Among the Yuanfeng attendants, many could be used;
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing was appointed military commissioner of Shu, Dao said, "Among the Yuanfeng court attendants, many men could serve;

sentences.zh: 惟京輕險貪愎，不可用。」

translations.literal: only Jing is frivolous, treacherous, greedy, and obstinate—he cannot be used."
translations.idiomatic: only Jing is reckless, treacherous, greedy, and stubborn—he must not be used."

sentences.zh: 又與同列議夏國地界，不能合，遂丐去。

translations.literal: He also joined his colleagues in deliberating the border with Western Xia but could not reach agreement, and so requested to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: He also deliberated with his colleagues over the border with Western Xia but could not reach agreement, and so asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 哲宗遣近臣問所以去意，且令密訪人才。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong sent a close attendant to ask the reason for his departure and also ordered him secretly to recommend men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhezong sent a close attendant to inquire why he wished to leave and also instructed him secretly to recommend men of talent.

sentences.zh: 燾曰：「信任不篤，言不見聽，而詢問人才，非臣所敢當也。」

translations.literal: Dao said, "Your Majesty's trust is not deep, and my words are not heeded—how dare I presume to answer when asked about men of talent?"
translations.idiomatic: Dao said, "Your Majesty's trust is not firm, and my counsel goes unheard—how dare I take it upon myself to recommend men of talent?"

sentences.zh: 使者再至，乃言：「人才可大任者，陛下自知之。

translations.literal: When the envoy came a second time, he then said, "As for men capable of great responsibility, Your Majesty knows them yourself.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy came again, he finally said, "As for men fit for great responsibility, Your Majesty already knows them yourself.

sentences.zh: 但須識別邪正，公天下之善惡，圖任舊人中堅正純厚有人望者，不牽左右好惡之言以移聖意，天下幸甚。」

translations.literal: You need only distinguish the wicked from the upright, judge good and evil for the sake of the realm, entrust office to upright, sincere, and substantial men of standing among the veterans, and not let the likes and dislikes of those at your side shift the sacred mind—the realm would be greatly fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: You need only distinguish the wicked from the upright, weigh good and evil for the empire's sake, place trust in upright, sincere, and substantial veterans of proven standing, and refuse to let the private preferences of those at your side sway the imperial mind—the empire would be greatly fortunate."

sentences.zh: 燾自立朝，一以引援人物為意。

translations.literal: From the time Dao entered court service, he consistently made the promotion of worthy men his aim.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he entered court service, Dao consistently made the advancement of worthy men his chief concern.

sentences.zh: 在鄂作《薦士錄》，具載姓名。

translations.literal: While in E Prefecture he compiled the Record of Recommended Scholars, listing all their names in full.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in Ezhou he compiled the Record of Recommended Scholars, setting down every name in full.

sentences.zh: 客或見其書，曰：「公所植桃李，乘時而發，但不向人開耳。」

translations.literal: A guest who saw the book said, "The peach and plum trees you have planted will bloom in season—but they simply do not blossom for others to see."
translations.idiomatic: A visitor who saw the book remarked, "The peach and plum you have planted will bloom in their season—but you never show their blossoms to anyone."

sentences.zh: 燾笑曰：「燾出入侍從，至位執政，八年之間所薦，用之不盡，負愧多矣。」

translations.literal: Dao laughed and said, "From the time I entered attendance on the throne until I reached the highest office, in eight years the men I recommended could not all be used—I bear much shame for that."
translations.idiomatic: Dao laughed and said, "From my years in attendance at court until I reached the highest office, over eight years the men I recommended could not all be appointed—I have much to feel ashamed of."

sentences.zh: 其好賢樂善如此。

translations.literal: Such was his love of worthies and delight in goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his love of the worthy and delight in doing good.

sentences.zh: 王岩叟

translations.literal: Wang Yansou
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yansou

sentences.zh: 王岩叟，字彥霖，大名清平人。

translations.literal: Wang Yansou, courtesy name Yanlin, was a native of Qingping in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yansou, styled Yanlin, came from Qingping in Daming.

sentences.zh: 幼時，語未正已知文字。

translations.literal: In childhood, before his speech was fully formed, he already knew written characters.
translations.idiomatic: As a child, before he could even speak properly, he already knew written characters.

sentences.zh: 仁宗患詞賦致經術不明，初置明經科，岩叟年十八，鄉舉、省試、廷對皆第一。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong, concerned that the examination essays obscured classical learning, first established the Mingjing examination; Yansou, at eighteen, ranked first in the prefectural, provincial, and palace examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong, troubled that the examination essays were eclipsing classical learning, established the Mingjing degree for the first time; Yansou, at eighteen, took first place in the prefectural, provincial, and palace examinations.

sentences.zh: 調欒城簿、涇州推官，甫兩月，聞弟喪，棄官歸養。

translations.literal: He was appointed recorder of Luancheng and investigating officer of Jing Prefecture; after only two months he heard of his younger brother's death and abandoned his post to return home and mourn.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed recorder of Luancheng and investigating officer in Jingzhou; after only two months he learned of his younger brother's death, resigned his post, and returned home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，韓琦留守北京，以為賢，辟管勾國子監，又辟管勾安撫司機宜文字，監晉州折博、煉鹽務。

translations.literal: During the Xining era, Han Qi, holding the northern capital, considered him worthy and recruited him as administrator of the Directorate of Education; he was again recruited as administrator of the pacification commission's secretariat and supervisor of the Jin Prefecture salt monopoly and refining office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining period, Han Qi, serving as regent of the northern capital, recognized his talent and recruited him as administrator of the Directorate of Education; he was later recruited again as administrator of the pacification commission's secretariat and as supervisor of the Jinzhou salt monopoly and refining office.

sentences.zh: 韓絳代琦，復欲留用。

translations.literal: When Han Jiang replaced Qi, he again wished to retain Yansou in service.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Jiang succeeded Qi, he too wished to keep Yansou in service.

sentences.zh: 岩叟謝曰：「岩叟，魏公之客，不願出他門也。」

translations.literal: Yansou declined, saying, "Yansou is Duke Wei's client; I am unwilling to go out through another man's gate."
translations.idiomatic: Yansou declined, saying, "I am Duke Wei's client; I am not willing to enter service through another patron's gate."

sentences.zh: 士君子稱之。

translations.literal: Men of principle praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Men of principle praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 後知定州安喜縣，有法吏罷居鄉里，導人為訟，岩叟捕撻於市，眾皆竦然。

translations.literal: Later, as magistrate of Anxi in Ding Prefecture, he found a legal clerk who had been dismissed and was living in the countryside inducing people to bring lawsuits; Yansou had him seized and flogged in the marketplace, and the crowd was awestruck.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as magistrate of Anxi in Dingzhou, he discovered a dismissed legal clerk living in the countryside who was inciting people to sue; Yansou had him arrested and publicly flogged in the marketplace, and the crowd was struck with awe.

sentences.zh: 定守呂公著嘆曰：「此古良吏也。」

translations.literal: The prefect Lü Gongzhu exclaimed, "This is an official of the ancient type."
translations.idiomatic: The prefect Lü Gongzhu exclaimed, "This is an official in the old worthy style."

sentences.zh: 有詔近臣舉御史，舉者意屬岩叟而未及識，或謂可一往見。

translations.literal: An edict went out for close ministers to recommend censors; the recommender had Yansou in mind but had not yet met him, and some suggested he might pay a visit.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict called on close ministers to recommend censors, one recommender had Yansou in mind though he had not yet met him, and someone suggested he might pay Yansou a visit.

sentences.zh: 岩叟笑曰：「是所謂呈身御史也。」

translations.literal: Yansou laughed and said, "That is what they call a censor who presents himself for appointment."
translations.idiomatic: Yansou laughed and said, "That is what people call a censor who curries favor to win appointment."

sentences.zh: 卒不見。

translations.literal: He never went.
translations.idiomatic: He never went.

sentences.zh: 哲宗即位，用劉摯薦，為監察御史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong took the throne, he was appointed investigating censor on Liu Zhi's recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, he was appointed investigating censor on Liu Zhi's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 時六察尚未言事，岩叟入台之明日，即上書論社稷安危之計，在從諫用賢，不可以小利失民心。

translations.literal: At the time the Six Investigations had not yet begun to speak on affairs; the day after Yansou entered the Censorate he submitted a memorial on the plan for the state's safety and peril, holding that one must heed remonstrance and employ the worthy and must not lose the people's hearts for small gain.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Six Investigations had not yet begun to speak on state affairs; the day after Yansou entered the Censorate he submitted a memorial on the safety and peril of the realm, arguing that the court must heed remonstrance, employ the worthy, and never sacrifice the people's loyalty for petty advantage.

sentences.zh: 遂言役錢斂法太重，民力不勝，願復差法如嘉祐時。

translations.literal: Thereupon he stated that the method of collecting corvée tax money was too heavy and the people's strength could not bear it, and he wished to restore the quota system as in the Jiayou period.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to argue that the levy of corvée funds was excessively burdensome and beyond what the people could sustain, and urged a return to the quota system used in the Jiayou era.

sentences.zh: 又言河北榷鹽法尚行，民受其弊，貧者不復食。

translations.literal: He also said that the government salt monopoly in Hebei was still in force, the people suffered its harm, and the poor no longer ate salt.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that the state salt monopoly in Hebei remained in effect, afflicting the populace to the point that the poor could no longer afford salt.

sentences.zh: 錄大名刻石《仁宗詔書》以進，又以河北天下根本，自祖宗以來，推此為惠。

translations.literal: He copied the stone inscription of Emperor Renzong's edict at Daming and presented it, also stating that Hebei was the fundamental root of the empire and that since the founding ancestors they had extended this as a benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He had transcribed and submitted the stone-carved edict of Emperor Renzong at Daming, adding that Hebei was the empire's foundation—and that since the founding ancestors, the court had granted that region this very benefit.

sentences.zh: 願復其舊。

translations.literal: He wished to restore its former state.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the old arrangement be restored.

sentences.zh: 江西鹽害民，詔遣使者往視。

translations.literal: Salt in Jiangxi harmed the people; an edict dispatched envoys to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When the salt policy in Jiangxi was harming the people, the throne ordered envoys to inspect the situation.

sentences.zh: 岩叟曰：「一方病矣，必待使還而後改為，恐有不及被德澤而死者。

translations.literal: Yansou said: "One region is already sick—if we must wait for the envoys to return before making changes, I fear some will die before receiving the emperor's grace.
translations.idiomatic: Yansou said, "That region is already suffering. If we must wait for the envoys to return before altering policy, I fear some will die before they can receive imperial relief.

sentences.zh: 願亟罷之。」

translations.literal: He wished to abolish it immediately."
translations.idiomatic: He urged that it be abolished at once."

sentences.zh: 又極陳時事，以為「不絕害本，百姓無由樂生；

translations.literal: He also exhaustively set forth current affairs, holding that "unless the root of harm is cut off, the common people have no way to live in contentment;
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke at length on affairs of the day, arguing that "unless the sources of harm are eliminated, the people will have no path to a secure livelihood;

sentences.zh: 不屏群邪，太平終是難致。」

translations.literal: unless corrupt factions are removed, enduring peace will ultimately be hard to attain."
translations.idiomatic: and "unless wicked factions are driven from court, lasting peace will remain out of reach."

sentences.zh: 時下詔求民疾苦，四方爭以其情赴訴，所司憚於省錄，頗成壅滯。

translations.literal: At the time an edict had been issued seeking the people's hardships; from all quarters they competed to bring their grievances, but the responsible offices feared recording them, and considerable backlog resulted.
translations.idiomatic: Around that time the throne had issued an edict inviting reports of popular hardship, and people from every region rushed to lodge complaints—but the responsible offices shrank from recording them, and petitions piled up in backlog.

sentences.zh: 岩叟言：「不問則已，言則必行之。

translations.literal: Yansou said: "If you do not ask, that is one thing; but if you ask, you must act on it.
translations.idiomatic: Yansou said, "If the court will not inquire, so be it—but once it asks, it must follow through.

sentences.zh: 不然，天下之人必謂陛下以空言說之，後有詔令，孰肯取信？」

translations.literal: Otherwise, people throughout the realm will surely say Your Majesty offered empty words, and who afterward will trust any edict?"
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the people will take Your Majesty's words as mere rhetoric—and who will believe future edicts?"

sentences.zh: 李定不持所生母仇氏服，岩叟論其不孝，定遂分司。

translations.literal: Li Ding did not observe mourning for his birth mother Lady Chou; Yansou impeached his filial impiety, and Ding was assigned to an outside post.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ding had failed to wear mourning for his biological mother, Lady Chou. Yansou indicted him for filial impiety, and Li was relegated to an outside assignment.

sentences.zh: 宰相蔡確為裕陵復土使，還朝，以定策自居。

translations.literal: The chief minister Cai Que served as commissioner for re-interment at Yuling; returning to court, he claimed credit for deciding the succession.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Cai Que, who had served as commissioner for re-interring the remains at Emperor Shenzong's tomb, returned to court claiming credit for securing the succession.

sentences.zh: 岩叟曰：「陛下之立，以子繼父，百王不易之道。

translations.literal: Yansou said: "Your Majesty's establishment followed a son succeeding his father—the unchanging way of all kings.
translations.idiomatic: Yansou said, "Your Majesty's enthronement followed the immemorial principle of a son succeeding his father.

sentences.zh: 且太皇太后先定於中，而確敢貪天自伐。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Empress Dowager had already settled it within the palace, yet Que dared to claim Heaven's favor for himself and boast of his deeds.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager had already settled the matter within the palace—yet Cai dared to arrogate Heaven's credit to himself.

sentences.zh: 章惇讒賊狼戾，罔上蔽明，不忠之罪，蓋與確等。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun was a slanderous villain, violent and unruly, deceiving superiors and obscuring clarity; his crime of disloyalty was roughly equal to Que's.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun was a slanderous, ruthless schemer who deceived his sovereign and obscured the truth—his disloyalty was no less than Cai's.

sentences.zh: 近簾前爭役法，詞氣不遜，無事上之禮。

translations.literal: Recently before the curtain he argued over the corvée law with impertinent tone, showing none of the respect due a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago, in audience before the curtain, he had disputed the corvée law in insubordinate tones, without the deference owed a sovereign.

sentences.zh: 今聖政不出房闥，豈宜容此大奸猶在廊廟！」

translations.literal: Now that sage governance does not issue from the inner chambers, how can such great villains still be tolerated in the hall of state!"
translations.idiomatic: With sagely governance no longer confined to the inner quarters, how can such great villains remain in the halls of power?

sentences.zh: 於是二人相繼退斥。

translations.literal: Thereupon the two men were driven from office in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Both men were subsequently dismissed from court.

sentences.zh: 遷左司諫兼權給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Remonstrance Bureau remonstrator and concurrently acting Supervising Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to remonstrator in the Left Remonstrance Bureau and concurrently served as acting Supervising Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 時並命執政，其間有不協時望者，岩叟即繳錄黃，上疏諫。

translations.literal: At the time several appointments to the executive were issued together; when any did not accord with public expectation, Yansou would return the yellow draft and submit a memorial remonstrating.
translations.idiomatic: When several executive appointments were issued at once, Yansou would return any draft that fell short of public expectation and submit a remonstrance memorial.

sentences.zh: 既而命不由門下省以出，岩叟請對，言之益切。

translations.literal: Soon an appointment was issued without passing through the Secretariat; Yansou requested a private audience and spoke with growing urgency.
translations.idiomatic: When an appointment was then issued without routing through the Secretariat, Yansou requested a personal audience and spoke all the more forcefully.

sentences.zh: 退就閣上疏曰：「臣為諫官既當言，承乏給事又當駁，非臣好為高論，喜忤大臣，恐命令斜出，尤損紀綱。」

translations.literal: Retiring to his office he submitted a memorial saying: "As remonstrator I must speak when duty requires; as acting Supervising Secretariat drafter I must reject improper drafts—it is not that I love lofty talk or delight in offending great ministers, but I fear commands issued by irregular channels will especially damage institutional order."
translations.idiomatic: Back in his office he memorialized: "As remonstrator I am bound to speak out; as acting Supervising Secretariat drafter I am bound to reject improper drafts. This is not because I relish grandstanding or offending senior ministers—I fear that edicts issued by irregular channels will corrode institutional discipline above all."

sentences.zh: 疏凡八上，命竟寢。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted eight times in all, and the appointment was finally dropped.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted the memorial eight times in all, and the appointment was ultimately withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 又言：「三省胥吏，月饗厚奉，歲累優秩。

translations.literal: He also said: "Clerks of the Three Departments enjoy hefty monthly stipends and yearly accumulation of preferential rank.
translations.idiomatic: He also observed: "Clerks in the Three Departments receive generous monthly pay and accumulate preferential promotions year after year.

sentences.zh: 而朝廷每舉一事，輒計功論賞，不知平日祿賜，將焉用之？

translations.literal: Yet whenever the court undertakes any task, it immediately calculates merit and discusses rewards—does it not know what the ordinary salaries and grants are for?
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever the court undertakes any project, it immediately tallies merit and dispenses rewards—as though the routine salaries served no purpose.

sentences.zh: 姑息相承，流弊已極。

translations.literal: Indulgence passed from one to the next, and abuses had reached their limit.
translations.idiomatic: A culture of indulgence had compounded itself until the abuses were extreme.

sentences.zh: 望飭勵大臣，事為之制。」

translations.literal: He hoped ministers would be admonished and encouraged to establish regulations for such matters."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that senior ministers be urged to set firm rules governing such practices.

sentences.zh: 即詔裁抑僥倖，定為十七條。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued to curb opportunistic favor, establishing seventeen articles.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was promptly issued to curb opportunistic favoritism, codified in seventeen articles.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace censor.

sentences.zh: 兩省正言久闕，岩叟上疏曰：「國朝仿近古之制，諫臣才至六員，方之先王，已為至少。

translations.literal: The rectifiers of the Two Departments had long been vacant; Yansou submitted a memorial saying: "Our dynasty follows near-ancient institutions—remonstrators number only six, already the fewest compared with former kings.
translations.idiomatic: The rectifier posts in both departments had long stood vacant. Yansou memorialized: "Our dynasty follows institutions modeled on antiquity, yet remonstrators number only six—already fewer than under the sage kings of old.

sentences.zh: 今復虛而不除，臣所未諭。

translations.literal: Now they remain vacant without being filled—this your servant cannot comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: That they should stand vacant still is something I cannot understand.

sentences.zh: 豈以為治道已清，而無事於言邪？

translations.literal: Is it because governance is already clear and there is no need for remonstrance?
translations.idiomatic: Does the court believe governance is already perfected and no remonstrance is needed?

sentences.zh: 人材難稱，不若虛其位邪？

translations.literal: Or is it because suitable talent is hard to find, and it is better to leave the posts empty?
translations.idiomatic: Or is it because no worthy candidate has been found, and the posts are better left empty?

sentences.zh: 二者皆非臣所望於今日也。

translations.literal: Neither of these is what your servant hopes for in the present day.
translations.idiomatic: Neither explanation is what I would hope for in our present age.

sentences.zh: 願趣補其闕，多進正人以壯本朝；

translations.literal: He wished them urgently filled and more upright men advanced to strengthen the dynasty;
translations.idiomatic: I urge that the vacancies be filled promptly and upright men advanced to strengthen the court—

sentences.zh: 正人進，則小人自消矣。」

translations.literal: when upright men advance, petty men will naturally disappear."
translations.idiomatic: for when upright men rise, petty ones fade away of their own accord."

sentences.zh: 諸路水災，朝廷行振貸，戶部限以災傷過七分、民戶降四等始許之。

translations.literal: Flood disasters struck various circuits; the court undertook relief loans, but the Ministry of Revenue limited eligibility to cases where disaster damage exceeded seventy percent and households had dropped four tax grades.
translations.idiomatic: When flooding struck several circuits, the court authorized relief loans—but the Ministry of Revenue restricted them to cases where disaster losses exceeded seventy percent and households had fallen four tax grades.

sentences.zh: 岩叟言：「中戶以上，蓋亦艱食。

translations.literal: Yansou said: "Middle households and above also surely go short of food.
translations.idiomatic: Yansou said, "Households above the lowest rank are also going hungry.

sentences.zh: 乞毋問分數、等級，皆得貸，庶幾王澤無間，以召至和矣。」

translations.literal: He begged that regardless of percentage or grade, all might receive loans, so that the emperor's grace would be without distinction and supreme harmony might be summoned."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that loans be granted without regard to damage percentages or tax grades, so that imperial bounty reaches all without distinction and true harmony may be restored."

sentences.zh: 坐張舜民事，改起居舍人，不拜，以直集賢院知齊州。

translations.literal: Due to the Zhang Shunmin affair, he was changed to Diary Drafter but declined the appointment, and served as Hanlin associate and prefect of Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his involvement in the Zhang Shunmin case, he was reassigned as a diary drafter—but declined to accept—and served as a Hanlin associate while governing Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 請河北所言鹽法，行之京東。

translations.literal: He requested the salt policy he had advocated for Hebei be applied in Jingdong.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned that the salt policy he had proposed for Hebei be extended to Jingdong.

sentences.zh: 明年，復以起居舍人召。

translations.literal: The following year he was again summoned as diary drafter.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was summoned back as a diary drafter.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍邇英講，進讀《寶訓》，至節費，岩叟曰：「凡言節用，非偶節一事便能有濟。

translations.literal: Once while attending lecture in the Hall for Close Reading, reading from the Precious Admonitions, when they came to thrift in expenditure, Yansou said: "Whenever one speaks of economizing, it is not that saving on one item occasionally will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while lecturing in the Hall for Close Reading from the Precious Admonitions, they reached the passage on thrift. Yansou said, "Economizing cannot mean sporadically cutting a single expense and expecting results.

sentences.zh: 當每事以節儉為意，則積久累日，國用自饒。」

translations.literal: One must approach every matter with frugality in mind; then, accumulated over long days, state revenue will naturally become abundant."
translations.idiomatic: Every undertaking must be guided by thrift—and over time, state revenues will grow ample of themselves."

sentences.zh: 讀仁宗知人事，岩叟曰：「人主常欲虛心平意，無所偏系，觀事以理，則事之是非，人之邪正，自然可見。」

translations.literal: Reading of Emperor Renzong's understanding of personnel, Yansou said: "The ruler must constantly keep an empty mind and level heart, without partial attachment; viewing affairs through reason—then the right and wrong of matters and the upright and corrupt of men will naturally become visible."
translations.idiomatic: When they read of Emperor Renzong's insight into men, Yansou said, "A sovereign must cultivate an open mind and level heart, free of partiality. View affairs by reason alone, and the rights and wrongs of matters—and the integrity or corruption of men—will reveal themselves naturally."

sentences.zh: 司馬康講《洪范》，至「乂用三德」，哲宗曰：「止此三德，為更有德。」

translations.literal: Sima Kang lectured on the Hong Fan, coming to "governing through the three virtues"; Zhezong said: "Only these three virtues—are there no other virtues?"
translations.idiomatic: Sima Kang was lecturing on the Great Plan, at the passage on "governing through the three virtues," when Zhezong asked, "Are these three virtues the only ones—or are there more?"

sentences.zh: 蓋哲宗自臨御，淵默不言，岩叟喜聞之，因欲風諫，退而上疏曰：「三德者，人君之大本，得之則治，失之則亂，不可須臾去者也。

translations.literal: Since Zhezong had ascended the throne he had been deep and silent, speaking little; Yansou was glad to hear him and wished to offer indirect remonstrance; retiring he submitted a memorial saying: "The three virtues are the great foundation of a ruler—obtain them and there is order, lose them and there is disorder; they cannot be absent even for a moment.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhezong had begun to reign he had been unusually reserved and seldom spoke, so Yansou was heartened to hear him and set out to offer indirect remonstrance. After retiring he memorialized: "The three virtues are a ruler's supreme foundation—possess them and there is order, lose them and there is chaos. They cannot be set aside even for a moment.

sentences.zh: 臣請別而言之。

translations.literal: Your servant asks to speak of them separately.
translations.idiomatic: Allow me to treat each in turn.

sentences.zh: 夫明是非於朝廷之上，判忠邪於多士之間，不以順己而忘其惡，不以逆己而遺其善，私求不徇於所愛，公議不遷於所憎。

translations.literal: To clarify right and wrong within the court, distinguish loyalty from treachery among the many scholars, not forgetting someone's evil because they agree with you, not overlooking someone's good because they oppose you, not indulging private requests for those you favor, not shifting public judgment for those you hate—
translations.idiomatic: To discern right from wrong at court and loyalty from treachery among the officials; to remember a man's faults even when he agrees with you, and a man's virtues even when he opposes you; to refuse private favor for those you love, and hold public judgment firm even against those you hate—

sentences.zh: 竭誠盡節者，任之當勿二；

translations.literal: those who exhaust loyalty and fulfill integrity—assign them without hesitation;
translations.idiomatic: to appoint with undivided trust those who serve with whole-hearted loyalty;

sentences.zh: 罔上盜寵者，棄之當勿疑。

translations.literal: those who deceive superiors and steal favor—abandon them without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: and to cast aside without hesitation those who deceive their sovereign and claw for favor.

sentences.zh: 惜紀綱，謹法度，重典刑，戒姑息，此人主之正直也。

translations.literal: Cherishing institutional order, adhering strictly to law, valuing penal codes, guarding against indulgence—this is the ruler's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: To cherish institutional discipline, uphold law with rigor, treat punishments as weighty matters, and guard against undue leniency—this is the ruler's virtue of integrity.

sentences.zh: 遠聲色之好，絕盤游之樂，勇於救天下之弊，果於斷天下之疑，邪說不能移，非道不能說，此人主之剛德也。

translations.literal: Keeping distant from the love of music and beauty, cutting off the pleasures of hunting and gaming, brave in remedying the empire's abuses, resolute in resolving the empire's doubts, unmoved by heterodox doctrines, unpersuaded by what is not the Way—this is the ruler's firm virtue.
translations.idiomatic: To keep one's distance from sensual pleasures, renounce idle diversions, courageously remedy the empire's ills, and decisively cut through its uncertainties; to remain unmoved by heterodox doctrine and unpersuaded by what diverges from the Way—this is the ruler's virtue of firmness.

sentences.zh: 居萬乘之尊而不驕，享四海之富而不溢，聰明有餘而處之若不足，俊傑並用而求之如不及，虛心以訪道，屈己以從諫，懼若臨淵，怯若履薄，此人主之柔德也。

translations.literal: Occupying the dignity of the ten-thousand-chariot ruler without pride, enjoying the wealth of the four seas without excess, possessing more than enough intelligence yet comporting as if insufficient, employing outstanding men together and seeking them as if falling short, humbly inquiring after the Way, bending oneself to follow remonstrance, fearful as if facing an abyss, timid as if treading on thin ice—this is the ruler's gentle virtue.
translations.idiomatic: To hold the throne without arrogance, enjoy the empire's wealth without excess, possess ample wisdom yet comport oneself as though it were never enough; to employ the talented together and seek them as urgently as though falling short; to inquire humbly after the Way, bow to remonstrance, and stand in awe as if over an abyss, treading as if on thin ice—this is the ruler's virtue of gentleness.

sentences.zh: 三者足以盡天下之要，在陛下力行何如耳。」

translations.literal: These three are sufficient to encompass all that is essential under Heaven—it depends solely on how vigorously Your Majesty puts them into practice."
translations.idiomatic: These three virtues encompass all that matters under Heaven—it rests entirely on how resolutely Your Majesty puts them into practice.

sentences.zh: 岩叟因侍講，奏曰：「陛下退朝無事，不知何以消日？」

translations.literal: Yansou, while serving as lecturer, memorialized saying: "When Your Majesty retires from court with nothing to do, how do you pass the day?"
translations.idiomatic: During a lecture session, Yansou asked, "When Your Majesty withdraws from court with leisure time, how do you spend the day?"

sentences.zh: 哲宗曰：「看文字。

translations.literal: Zhezong said: "Reading texts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong replied, "Reading.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下以讀書為樂，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: He replied: "That Your Majesty takes reading as pleasure—under Heaven this is most fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Yansou answered, "That Your Majesty finds joy in reading is the good fortune of the realm.

sentences.zh: 聖賢之學，非造次可成，須在積累。

translations.literal: The learning of sages is not achieved in haste; it requires accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: The learning of the sages cannot be mastered overnight—it must be built up over time.

sentences.zh: 積累之要，在專與勤。

translations.literal: The key to accumulation lies in concentration and diligence.
translations.idiomatic: The keys to that accumulation are single-mindedness and persistence.

sentences.zh: 屏絕它好，始可謂之專；

translations.literal: Shutting out other loves—only then can one be called concentrated;
translations.idiomatic: Shut out other distractions—that is single-mindedness;

sentences.zh: 久而不倦，始可謂之勤。

translations.literal: persisting long without weariness—only then can one be called diligent.
translations.idiomatic: persevere without tiring—that is diligence.

sentences.zh: 願陛下特留聖意。」

translations.literal: He wished Your Majesty would especially retain this sage intent."
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will keep this specially in mind.

sentences.zh: 哲宗然之。

translations.literal: Zhezong assented.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong agreed.

sentences.zh: 岩叟館伴遼賀正旦使耶律寬，寬求觀《元會儀》，岩叟曰：「此非外國所宜知。」

translations.literal: Yansou served as host for the Liao envoy Yelü Kuan coming to congratulate the New Year; Kuan asked to view the New Year's Assembly rites; Yansou said: "This is not what foreign states ought to know."
translations.idiomatic: Yansou served as host to the Liao envoy Yelü Kuan, who had come to offer New Year's greetings. When Kuan asked to observe the New Year's Assembly rites, Yansou said, "That is not something a foreign envoy should be allowed to see."

sentences.zh: 止錄《笏記》與之，寬不敢求。

translations.literal: He only copied out the Court Record notes and gave them to him; Kuan did not dare ask further.
translations.idiomatic: He provided only a copy of the court ceremonial memorandum—and Kuan did not dare press the matter.

sentences.zh: 進權吏部侍郎、天章閣待制、樞密都承旨。

translations.literal: He was promoted to acting Vice Minister of Personnel, Hanlin Academy attendant, and chief clerk of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting vice minister of personnel, Hanlin attendant, and chief clerk of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 湖北諸蠻互出擾邊，無有寧歲，岩叟請專以疆事委荊南唐義問。

translations.literal: Various Man tribes in Hubei raided the borders in turn, with no peaceful year; Yansou requested that frontier affairs be entrusted exclusively to Tang Yiwen of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Man tribes in Hubei raided the frontier in turn, year after year without respite. Yansou urged that border affairs be entrusted entirely to Tang Yiwen at Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 遂自草檄文，喻義問以朝廷方敦尚恩信，勿為僥倖功賞之意，後遂安輯。

translations.literal: Thereupon he himself drafted a proclamation, instructing Yiwen that the court was now promoting grace and trustworthiness and should not seek opportunistic merit and rewards; afterward the region was settled.
translations.idiomatic: He himself drafted the proclamation, instructing Yiwen that the court was committed to grace and good faith—not opportunistic raids for merit—and the region was subsequently pacified.

sentences.zh: 初，夏人遣使入貢，及為境上之議，故為此去彼來，牽致勞苦，每違期日。

translations.literal: Initially, when the Western Xia sent envoys to pay tribute and when border negotiations were conducted, they arranged come-and-go alternation, causing strain and hardship and often missing deadlines.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Western Xia sent tribute missions or negotiated border matters, they insisted on alternating which side crossed the frontier—a burdensome arrangement that often led to missed deadlines.

sentences.zh: 岩叟請預戒邊臣，夏違期，一不至則勿復應，自後不復敢違。

translations.literal: Yansou requested that frontier officials be warned in advance: if Xia violated the deadline even once and failed to come, no further response should be made—and thereafter they did not dare violate again.
translations.idiomatic: Yansou proposed that frontier officials be instructed in advance: if the Xia missed a deadline even once, the court should cease responding—and from then on they did not dare miss again.

sentences.zh: 質孤、勝如二堡，漢趙充國留屯之所，自元祐講和，在蘭州界內，夏以為形勝膏腴之地，力爭之。

translations.literal: The two forts Zhigu and Shengru were places where the Han general Zhao Chongguo had garrisoned; since the Yuanyou peace agreement they lay within Lanzhou's borders, but Xia regarded them as strategically advantageous and fertile land and contested them fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: The forts of Zhigu and Shengru, where the Han general Zhao Chongguo had once stationed troops, lay within Lanzhou's borders after the Yuanyou peace—but the Xia considered them strategically vital, fertile ground and contested them fiercely.

sentences.zh: 二堡若失，則蘭州、熙河遂危。

translations.literal: If the two forts were lost, Lanzhou and Xihe would then be endangered.
translations.idiomatic: Lose those two forts and Lanzhou and Xihe would be imperiled.

sentences.zh: 延帥欲以二堡與夏，蘇轍主其議。

translations.literal: The Yanzhou commander wished to cede the two forts to Xia; Su Zhe championed this proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The commander of Yanzhou wanted to surrender the two forts to the Xia, and Su Zhe led the faction supporting the idea.

sentences.zh: 及熙河、延安二捷同報，轍奏曰：「近邊奏稍頻，西人意在得二堡。

translations.literal: When victories at Xihe and Yan'an were reported together, Zhe memorialized saying: "Recent frontier reports have come somewhat frequently; the Westerners' intent is to obtain the two forts.
translations.idiomatic: When news of victories at Xihe and Yan'an arrived together, Su Zhe memorialized: "Frontier reports have lately been frequent—the Western Xia's aim is to secure those two forts.

sentences.zh: 今盛夏猶如此，入秋可虞，不若早定議。」

translations.literal: Even in midsummer it is still like this; entering autumn gives cause for concern—it would be better to settle the matter early."
translations.idiomatic: If they are this aggressive in high summer, autumn will be worse—it is better to reach a decision now."

sentences.zh: 意在與之也。

translations.literal: His intent was to cede them.
translations.idiomatic: His meaning was to give the forts up.

sentences.zh: 岩叟曰：「形勢之地，豈可輕棄，不知既與，還不更求否？」

translations.literal: Yansou said: "Strategic terrain—how can it be lightly abandoned? Once ceded, will they not seek more?"
translations.idiomatic: Yansou said, "How can we lightly surrender such strategic ground? Once we yield it, will they not demand more?"

sentences.zh: 太皇太后曰：「然。」

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager said: "Indeed."
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager agreed: "Exactly so."

sentences.zh: 議遂止。

translations.literal: The deliberation thereupon ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 夏人數萬侵定西之東、通遠之北，壞七厓匙堡，掠居人，轉侵涇原及河外鄜、府州，眾遂至十萬。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of Xia troops invaded east of Dingxi and north of Tongyuan, destroyed the Qiyanshi Fort, plundered inhabitants, then turned to raid Jingyuan and Fuzhou and other prefectures beyond the river until their numbers reached one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of Xia troops invaded east of Dingxi and north of Tongyuan, destroyed Qiyanshi Fort, pillaged local inhabitants, and swept on into Jingyuan and the prefectures of Fu and Fuzhou beyond the river, until their forces reached one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 熙帥范育偵伺夏右廂種落大抵趣河外，三疏請乘此進堡砦，築龕谷、勝如、相照、定西而東徑隴諾城。

translations.literal: Fan Yu, commander of Xi Prefecture, reconnoitered that Xia's Right Wing tribes were mostly heading beyond the river; thrice he memorialized requesting to take advantage and advance forts, building at Kangu, Shengru, Xiangzhao, and east from Dingxi via Longnuo City.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi Prefecture commander Fan Yu detected that most of the Xia Right Wing tribes were heading beyond the river and thrice petitioned to seize the moment and advance with new fortifications—building at Kangu, Shengru, Xiangzhao, and east from Dingxi through to Longnuo City.

sentences.zh: 朝議未一，或欲以七巉經毀之地，皆以與夏。

translations.literal: Court opinion was not unified; some wished to cede to Xia all the territory of the seven precipitous cliffs that had been ravaged.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion was divided; some argued that all the ravaged territory around the Seven Cliffs should be surrendered to the Xia.

sentences.zh: 岩叟力言不可與，彼計得行，後患未已。

translations.literal: Yansou strongly argued they must not be ceded; if the enemy's plan succeeded, later troubles would not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yansou insisted they must not be surrendered—if the enemy's scheme succeeded, trouble would never end.

sentences.zh: 因請遣官諭熙帥，即以戶部員外郎穆衍行視，築定遠以據要害。

translations.literal: Thereupon he requested an official be sent to instruct the Xi commander; the Ministry of Revenue vice director Mu Yan was dispatched to inspect on-site and build Dingyuan to hold the key positions.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned that an official be sent to instruct the Xi commander, and Mu Yan of the Ministry of Revenue was dispatched on an inspection tour to build Dingyuan and hold the key positions.

sentences.zh: 其調兵貲費，一從便宜，不必中覆。

translations.literal: Troop deployments and expenditures were all handled as circumstances required, without needing central review.
translations.idiomatic: Troop deployments and expenditures were to be managed as local circumstances required, without awaiting central approval.

sentences.zh: 定遠遂城，皆岩叟之力。

translations.literal: Dingyuan was successfully fortified—all through Yansou's efforts.
translations.idiomatic: The fortification of Dingyuan was entirely due to Yansou's efforts.

sentences.zh: 拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed as a Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 滕甫帥太原，為走馬承受所撼，徙潁昌。

translations.literal: Teng Fu commanded Taiyuan and was shaken by the roaming inspector; he was transferred to Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Fu, commanding Taiyuan, was undermined by a roaming inspector and was transferred to Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 岩叟封還詞頭，言：「進退帥臣，理宜重慎。

translations.literal: Yansou sealed and returned the draft appointment, saying: "Advancing and retiring frontier commanders should by reason be weighed with great caution.
translations.idiomatic: Yansou returned the draft appointment unapproved, stating: "The appointment and removal of frontier commanders ought to be weighed with the utmost care.

sentences.zh: 今以小臣一言易之，使後人畏憚不自保，此風浸長，非委任安邊之福。」

translations.literal: Now to change it on one minor official's word makes later men fearful and unable to protect themselves; as this practice spreads, it is no blessing for entrusting and securing the borders."
translations.idiomatic: To transfer a commander on a single underling's word will make future appointees live in fear for their posts. As this practice spreads, it bodes ill for stable frontier command."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: It was thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The transfer was halted.

sentences.zh: 復為樞密都承旨、權知開封府。

translations.literal: He again served as chief clerk of the Bureau of Military Affairs and acting prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as chief clerk of the Bureau of Military Affairs while acting as prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 舊以推、判官二人分左右廳，共治一事，多為異同，或累日不竟，吏疲於咨稟。

translations.literal: Formerly two chief deputies and judges divided the left and right offices and jointly handled single matters, often disagreeing, sometimes not finishing for days—clerks were exhausted from reporting back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, two deputy administrators and judges split the left and right offices and jointly handled every case, often disagreeing—cases could drag on for days, and clerks were worn down by the constant back-and-forth.

sentences.zh: 岩叟創立逐官分治之法，自是署為令。

translations.literal: Yansou established the method of having each official handle matters separately; from then it became regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Yansou instituted a system whereby each official handled cases separately—and it became standing practice.

sentences.zh: 都城群偷所聚，謂之「大房」，每區容數十百人，淵藪詭僻，不可勝究。

translations.literal: Thieves in the capital gathered in groups called "great houses," each district holding scores or hundreds of men, in deep lairs hidden and remote, beyond full investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Thieves in the capital gathered in dens they called "great houses," each large enough for scores or even hundreds of men—hidden lairs in labyrinthine quarters beyond thorough policing.

sentences.zh: 岩叟令掩捕撤毀，隨輕重決之，根株一空。

translations.literal: Yansou ordered secret arrests and destruction of the dens, judging according to severity until the roots were entirely cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Yansou ordered raids to destroy these dens, punishing offenders according to severity until the entire network was uprooted.

sentences.zh: 供備庫使曹續以產貿萬緡，市儈逾年負其半，續儘力不可取。

translations.literal: Cao Xu, commissioner of the Commissary Depot, had sold property for ten thousand strings of cash; the merchant owed him half for over a year, and Xu exhausted every means but could not collect.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xu, commissioner of the Commissary Depot, had sold property for ten thousand strings of cash; the buyer still owed half after more than a year, and despite every effort Xu could not collect the debt.

sentences.zh: 一日啟戶，則所負皆在焉。

translations.literal: One day he opened the door, and all that was owed was there.
translations.idiomatic: One day when he opened his door, the full sum owed had been placed there.

sentences.zh: 驚扣其故，儈曰：「王公今日知府矣。」

translations.literal: Startled, he asked the reason; the merchant said: "Lord Wang became prefect today."
translations.idiomatic: Astonished, he asked how this had happened. The merchant replied, "Lord Wang was appointed prefect today."

sentences.zh: 初，曹氏之隸韓絢與同隸訟，事連其主，就逮之。

translations.literal: Initially, Han Xuan, a bondservant of the Cao clan, sued a fellow bondservant; the case implicated his master, who was taken into custody.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Han Xuan, a bondservant of the Cao family, had brought suit against another bondservant; because the matter implicated his master, the master was arrested.

sentences.zh: 曹氏者，慈聖後之族也。

translations.literal: The Cao clan were relatives of Empress Dowager Cisheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Cao clan were kin of Empress Dowager Cisheng.

sentences.zh: 岩叟言：「部曲相訟，不當論其主。

translations.literal: Yansou said: "When household retainers sue one another, their master ought not to be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Yansou argued, "When retainers bring lawsuits against one another, their lord should not be put on trial.

sentences.zh: 今不惟長告訐之風，且傷孝治。

translations.literal: Now it not only encourages the practice of informing and denunciation, but also harms governance by filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: To proceed would not only nourish the habit of denunciation—it would also undermine a reign grounded in filial virtue.

sentences.zh: 慈聖仙游未遠，一旦因廝役之過，使其子孫對吏，殆聖情有所不忍。」

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Cisheng's ascension to heaven was not long past; to have her descendants face officials all at once because of a menial's fault—surely the sage feelings could hardly bear it."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Cisheng has only lately passed away. To drag her descendants before the magistrates over a servant's offense—the sage woman's heart would scarcely endure it."

sentences.zh: 詔竄絢而絕其獄。

translations.literal: An edict exiled Han Xuan and terminated the case.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial decree banished Han Xuan and closed the case.

sentences.zh: 岩叟常謂：「天下積欠多名，催免不一，公私費擾，乞隨等第多寡為催法。」

translations.literal: Yansou often said: "Throughout the realm accumulated arrears have many names; collection and remission are inconsistent, troubling both public and private affairs. I request that collection methods be set according to rank and amount owed."
translations.idiomatic: Yansou had long urged, "Arrears across the empire are recorded under countless names, with collection and remission applied unevenly, bedeviling both government and populace. I ask that collection be regulated according to rank and the size of the debt."

sentences.zh: 朝廷乃定五年十科之令。

translations.literal: The court thereupon established the five-year, ten-installment order.
translations.idiomatic: The court accordingly promulgated the rule of collection in ten installments over five years.

sentences.zh: 元祐六年，拜樞密直學士、簽書院事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanyou, he was appointed Privy Council Academician and Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Yuanyou reign, he received appointment as Privy Council Academician and Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 入謝，太皇太后曰：「知卿才望，不次超用。」

translations.literal: Upon entering to give thanks, the Grand Empress Dowager said: "I know your talent and reputation and have promoted you beyond ordinary precedence."
translations.idiomatic: When he came to give thanks for the appointment, the Grand Empress Dowager said, "Knowing your talent and standing, I have advanced you out of turn."

sentences.zh: 岩叟又再拜謝，進曰：「太后聽政以來，納諫從善，務合人心，所以朝廷清明，天下安靜。

translations.literal: Yansou bowed again in thanks and advanced, saying: "Since Your Majesty began administering the government, you have accepted remonstrance and followed what is good, striving to accord with the hearts of the people—thus the court is clear and bright, and the realm tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Yansou bowed low again and stepped forward. "Since Your Majesty took up the regency, you have heeded counsel and embraced what is right, striving always to align with the people's hearts. That is why the court is upright and the realm at peace.

sentences.zh: 願信之勿疑，守之勿失。」

translations.literal: I hope you will trust this and not doubt; hold to it and do not lose it."
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to believe in this without doubt and to hold to it without letting it slip."

sentences.zh: 復少進而西，奏哲宗曰：「陛下今日聖學，當深辨邪正。

translations.literal: Then he stepped forward a little to the west and addressed Emperor Zhezong: "Your Majesty's sagely learning today should deeply distinguish the wicked from the upright.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved a few steps westward and addressed Emperor Zhezong. "In Your Majesty's studies today, you must learn to discern clearly the upright from the wicked.

sentences.zh: 正人在朝，則朝廷安，邪人一進，便有不安之象。

translations.literal: When upright men are at court, the court is secure; when a wicked man enters, there at once appears an inauspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: When upright men hold office, the court is secure; let but one wicked man slip in, and signs of disorder appear at once.

sentences.zh: 非謂一夫能然，蓋其類應之者眾，上下蔽蒙，不覺養成禍胎爾。」

translations.literal: I do not mean that a single man could do this—rather, his kind respond in multitudes; above and below are blinded and deceived, unwittingly nurturing the embryo of disaster."
translations.idiomatic: I do not mean that one man alone can bring this about—but his kind rally in numbers; court and countryside fall under a fog, and before anyone notices, the seeds of calamity have been sown."

sentences.zh: 又進曰：「或聞有以君子小人參用之說告陛下者，不知果有之否？

translations.literal: He advanced again, saying: "I have heard that someone may have told Your Majesty that upright men and petty men should be employed together—I wonder whether this is indeed so?
translations.idiomatic: He stepped forward once more. "I have heard it rumored that someone has advised Your Majesty to employ upright men and petty men side by side—I do not know whether there is any truth to this.

sentences.zh: 此乃深誤陛下也。

translations.literal: This deeply misleads Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Such counsel deeply misleads Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 自古君子小人，無參用之理。

translations.literal: From antiquity, upright men and petty men have had no principle of joint employment.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, there has never been sound reason to employ upright men and petty men together.

sentences.zh: 聖人但云：『君子在內，小人在外則泰，小人在內、君子在外則否。」

translations.literal: The sage merely said: "When upright men are within and petty men without, there is peace; when petty men are within and upright men without, there is decline."
translations.idiomatic: The sages say only this: "When upright men are within and petty men without, there is prosperity; when petty men are within and upright men without, there is ruin."

sentences.zh: 小人既進，君子必引類而去。

translations.literal: Once petty men enter, upright men must gather their kind and depart.
translations.idiomatic: Once petty men gain entry, upright men inevitably withdraw—and their allies go with them.

sentences.zh: 若君子與小人競進，則危亡之基也。

translations.literal: If upright men and petty men vie to enter together, that is the foundation of peril and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Should upright men and petty men compete for office together, that is the groundwork of national collapse.

sentences.zh: 此際不可不察。」

translations.literal: At this juncture one cannot fail to examine it.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty must heed this moment with utmost care.

sentences.zh: 兩宮深然之。

translations.literal: Both palaces deeply assented to this.
translations.idiomatic: Both the Grand Empress Dowager and the Emperor found his words deeply convincing.

sentences.zh: 上清儲詳宮成，太皇太后謂輔臣曰：「此與皇帝皆出閣中物營之，以成先帝之志。」

translations.literal: When the Shangqing Chuxiang Palace was completed, the Grand Empress Dowager told the chief ministers: "This and the emperor's [project] were both built from items stored in the inner pavilion, to fulfill the late emperor's will."
