translations.idiomatic: When the Shangqing Chuxiang Palace was completed, the Grand Empress Dowager told the chief ministers, "This palace, like the emperor's own quarters, was built entirely from goods already held in the inner storehouses—to fulfill the late emperor's wish."

sentences.zh: 岩叟曰：「陛下不煩公，不勞民，真盛德事。

translations.literal: Yansou said: "Your Majesty has not troubled the treasury nor wearied the people—this is truly a deed of surpassing virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yansou replied, "Your Majesty has accomplished this without burdening the state coffers or exhausting the people—a deed of truly great virtue.

sentences.zh: 然願自今以土木為戒。」

translations.literal: Yet I hope that from now on you will take earth-and-timber construction as a warning."
translations.idiomatic: Yet I pray that from this day forward Your Majesty will treat such building projects as a warning."

sentences.zh: 又以宮成將戒肆赦，岩叟曰：「昔天禧中，祥源成，治平中，醴泉成，皆未嘗赦。

translations.literal: Also, when the palace was completed they were about to proclaim a general amnesty; Yansou said: "Formerly in the Tianxi era, when Xiangyuan was completed; in the Zhiping era, when Liquan was completed—neither occasion was marked by amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace's completion was to be marked by a general amnesty, Yansou objected: "In the Tianxi era, when Xiangyuan Palace was finished, and in the Zhiping era, when Liquan Palace was finished—neither was celebrated with an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 古人有垂死諫君無赦者，此可見赦無益於聖治也。」

translations.literal: There were ancients who, on their deathbeds, remonstrated with their lords against amnesty—this shows that amnesty does not benefit sage governance."
translations.idiomatic: There were ancients who, even on their deathbeds, urged their rulers not to grant amnesties—clear proof that pardons do nothing for enlightened rule."

sentences.zh: 哲宗方選後，太皇太后曰：「今得狄諮女，年命以便，然為是庶出過房，事須評議。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong was selecting an empress; the Grand Empress Dowager said: "We now have Di Zi's daughter—the age and fate are convenient—but as she is of concubine birth and was adopted out, the matter must be deliberated."
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Zhezong was choosing an empress, the Grand Empress Dowager said, "We have settled on the daughter of Di Zi—her age and horoscope are suitable—but she was born to a concubine and given in adoption elsewhere. The matter requires careful discussion."

sentences.zh: 岩叟進曰：「按《禮經·問名篇》，女家答曰：『臣女，夫婦所生。』

translations.literal: Yansou advanced, saying: "According to the 'Inquiry of Names' chapter of the Book of Rites, the bride's family replies: 'My daughter, born to husband and wife.
translations.idiomatic: Yansou stepped forward. "According to the 'Inquiry of Names' chapter of the Book of Rites, when asked the bride's name the family replies, 'My daughter, born of our lawful union.

sentences.zh: 及外氏官諱，不識今者狄氏將何辭以進？」

translations.literal: And as for taboo names in the maternal family's official titles—I do not know what words the Di clan will use when presenting her?"
translations.idiomatic: As for taboo names connected with the maternal family's official posts—I wonder what language the Di family could use in presenting her?"

sentences.zh: 議遂寢。

translations.literal: The deliberation was thereupon shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The deliberations were dropped.

sentences.zh: 哲宗選後既定，太皇太后曰：「帝得賢后，有內助功，不是小事。」

translations.literal: Once Emperor Zhezong's empress was settled, the Grand Empress Dowager said: "The emperor gaining a worthy empress—there is merit in domestic support; it is no small matter."
translations.idiomatic: After the empress was finally chosen, the Grand Empress Dowager remarked, "For the emperor to gain a worthy consort, with all the benefit that brings within the palace—this is no trivial matter."

sentences.zh: 岩叟對曰：「內助雖後事，其正家須在皇帝。

translations.literal: Yansou replied: "Though domestic support comes later, rectifying the family must rest with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yansou answered, "Domestic support may come afterward, but ordering the household properly falls to the emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 聖人言：『正家而得天下』。

translations.literal: The sage said: 'Rectify the family and you gain the realm.'
translations.idiomatic: The sage says, 'Rectify the family, and you will secure the realm.'

sentences.zh: 當慎之於始。」

translations.literal: One must be cautious at the beginning."
translations.idiomatic: Caution is needed from the very beginning."

sentences.zh: 太皇太后以是語哲宗者再。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager repeated these words to Emperor Zhezong.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager repeated this counsel to Emperor Zhezong more than once.

sentences.zh: 岩叟退取歷代後事可為法者，類為《中宮懿范》上之。

translations.literal: Yansou retired and gathered precedents concerning empresses through the ages that could serve as models, classified them as "Imperial Models of Virtue in the Inner Palace," and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Yansou withdrew and compiled exemplary precedents concerning empresses from dynastic history into a work titled Imperial Models of Virtue for the Inner Palace, which he presented to the throne.

sentences.zh: 宰相劉摯、右丞蘇轍以人言求避位，岩叟曰：「元祐之初，排斥奸邪，緝熙聖治，摯與轍之功居多。

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Liu Zhe and Vice Grand Councilor Su Che, on account of people's words, sought to resign; Yansou said: "At the beginning of Yuanyou, in expelling the treacherous and wicked and extending sagely governance, Zhe and Che's contributions were foremost.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Councilor Liu Zhe and Vice Grand Councilor Su Che asked to step down amid public criticism, Yansou argued, "At the outset of the Yuanyou era, in rooting out the corrupt and restoring enlightened governance, no one contributed more than Zhe and Che.

sentences.zh: 原深察讒毀之意，重惜腹心之人，無輕其去就。」

translations.literal: I pray you will deeply examine the intent behind slander, greatly cherish those who are closest to your heart, and not lightly treat their departure or retention."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesties to see through the malice behind these attacks and to hold fast to your most trusted advisers—do not treat their standing lightly."

sentences.zh: 兩宮然之。

translations.literal: Both palaces assented.
translations.idiomatic: Both the Grand Empress Dowager and the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 後摯竟為御史鄭雍所擊，岩叟連上疏論救。

translations.literal: Later Zhe was indeed attacked by Censor Zheng Yong; Yansou submitted memorials in succession arguing for his rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhe was eventually attacked by Censor Zheng Yong, and Yansou repeatedly submitted memorials in his defense.

sentences.zh: 摯去位，御史遂指為黨，罷為端明殿學士、知鄭州。

translations.literal: Zhe left office; the censors then denounced him as factional and removed him to Academician of the Hall of Manifest Brightness and prefect of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhe left office, the censorate denounced him as a factional leader and demoted him to Academician of the Hall of Manifest Brightness and prefect of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 言者猶未厭，太皇太后曰：「岩叟有大功，今日之命，出不獲已耳。」

translations.literal: The critics were still unsatisfied; the Grand Empress Dowager said: "Yansou has great merit; today's appointment was made with no other choice."
translations.idiomatic: The accusers were still not satisfied. The Grand Empress Dowager said, "Yansou has rendered great service. Today's order was issued only because we had no choice."

sentences.zh: 明年，徙河陽，數月卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Heyang; several months later he died, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Heyang; within a few months he died, at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈左正議大夫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Left Direct Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Left Direct Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，追貶雷州別駕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng, he was posthumously demoted to Vice-Prefect of Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shaosheng era, his posthumous honors were revoked and he was degraded to Vice-Prefect of Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 司馬光以其進諫無隱，稱之曰：「吾寒心栗齒，憂在不測，公處之自如，至於再三，或累十數章，必行其言而後已。」

translations.literal: Sima Guang, because of his unreserved remonstrance, praised him, saying: "My heart chilled and teeth chattered, fearing the unforeseen; the lord handled it at ease—to the point of doing it two or three times, sometimes accumulating a dozen or more chapters, not stopping until his words were carried out."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang, speaking of his fearless candor in remonstrance, praised him thus: "I myself trembled with fear of what might come—and yet you remonstrated with perfect calm, submitting again and again, sometimes a dozen memorials in succession, never resting until your counsel was heeded."

sentences.zh: 為文語省理該，深得制誥體。

translations.literal: His writings were economical in language, comprehensive in reasoning, deeply mastering the diction of imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was spare yet comprehensive in argument, in full mastery of the edict form.

sentences.zh: 有《易》、《詩》、《春秋傳》行於世。

translations.literal: He had Commentaries on the Changes, the Odes, and the Spring and Autumn Annals circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His commentaries on the Book of Changes, the Book of Odes, and the Spring and Autumn Annals circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 鄭雍，字公肅，襄邑人。

translations.literal: Zheng Yong, styled Gongsu, was a native of Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yong, courtesy name Gongsu, was a native of Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 進士甲科，調兗州推官。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the first rank and was appointed judicial assistant of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He placed in the top tier of the jinshi examination and was assigned as judicial assistant in Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 韓琦上其文，召試秘閣校理、知太常禮院。

translations.literal: Han Qi presented his writings; he was summoned to examination and appointed Collator of the Secretariat Archive and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi forwarded his writings to the throne; Zheng was summoned for examination and appointed Collator of the Secretariat Archive and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 英宗之喪，論宗室不當嫁娶，與時相忤，通判峽州，知池州，復還太常禮院，歷開封府判官。

translations.literal: During Emperor Yingzong's mourning, he argued that imperial clansmen ought not to marry; this opposed the chief ministers; he was made vice-prefect of Xia Prefecture, prefect of Chi Prefecture, returned to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and served as judicial administrator of the Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the mourning period for Emperor Yingzong, he argued that members of the imperial clan should not marry—a position that put him at odds with the chief ministers. He was transferred to vice-prefect of Xia Prefecture, then prefect of Chi Prefecture, then recalled to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and eventually served as judicial administrator of the Kaifeng Prefecture government.

sentences.zh: 熙寧、元豐間，更制變令，士大夫多違己以求合，雍獨靜默自守。

translations.literal: Between the Xining and Yuanfeng eras, as regulations were repeatedly changed, many literati-officials abandoned their principles to seek conformity; Yong alone silently held to himself.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining and Yuanfeng periods, as reforms and regulations shifted repeatedly, most scholar-officials bent their principles to stay in favor—but Zheng Yong alone held his silence and his integrity.

sentences.zh: 改嘉王、岐王府記室參軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be secretary to the households of Princes Jia and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as secretary in the households of Princes Jia and Qi.

sentences.zh: 神宗末年，二王既長，猶居禁中，雍獻四箴規戒，且諷使求出外邸。

translations.literal: In the final years of Emperor Shenzong, the two princes though grown still resided within the forbidden precincts; Yong submitted four admonitions of restraint and, moreover, subtly urged them to seek residence in outer mansions.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenzong's final years, though both princes had come of age, they still lived within the palace precincts. Zheng submitted four admonitory essays and delicately urged them to request quarters outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 凡在邸七年，用久次，以轉運使秩留。

translations.literal: In all he was at the mansions seven years; by virtue of long seniority he was retained at the rank of transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He remained at the princes' mansions for seven years in all, and by seniority of service was retained at the rank of transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 宣仁後知其賢，及臨政，擢為起居郎，進中書舍人。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuanren knew his worth; when she assumed governance she promoted him to Palace Diarist and advanced him to Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuanren, recognizing his talent, elevated him to Palace Diarist when she took power, then promoted him to Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 鄧潤甫除翰林承旨，雍當制。

translations.literal: Deng Runfu was appointed Hanlin Academy Chief Academician; Yong was to draft the appointment edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Runfu was appointed Chief Academician of the Hanlin Academy, Zheng Yong was assigned to draft the appointment edict.

sentences.zh: 制未出，言事者五人交章攻之，換為侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Before the edict was issued, five memorialists submitted overlapping memorials attacking him; [Deng] was replaced as Lecturer Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict could be issued, five memorialists submitted overlapping attacks on the appointment, and Deng was given the lesser post of Lecturer Academician instead.

sentences.zh: 雍言：二職皆天下精選，以潤甫之過薄，不當革前命；

translations.literal: Yong said: Both posts are the finest selections in the realm; given Runfu's slight faults, the prior appointment ought not to be revoked;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yong argued: "Both offices represent the most select appointments in the realm. Given the minor nature of Runfu's faults, the original appointment should not have been overturned;

sentences.zh: 以為奸邪，不當在經幄。

translations.literal: regarding him as treacherous and wicked, he ought not to be at the imperial lecture hall.
translations.idiomatic: and if he is truly wicked, he ought not to serve in the imperial lecture hall at all.

sentences.zh: 今中外咸謂朝廷姑以是塞言者，如此則邪正何由可辨，善惡何由可明？

translations.literal: Now inside and outside all say the court is merely using this to silence the critics—if so, how can wicked and upright be distinguished, how can good and evil be made clear?
translations.idiomatic: Now court and countryside alike believe the court merely offered this compromise to silence critics. But if that is so, how are the wicked to be distinguished from the upright, and good from evil?

sentences.zh: 若每事必待言，是賞罰之柄，不得已而行，非所以示信天下之道。」

translations.literal: If every matter must await remonstrance, then the power of reward and punishment is exercised only when compelled—this is not the way to show faith to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: If every decision must wait for criticism before it is corrected, then reward and punishment are wielded only under duress—not the way to inspire confidence throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 潤甫仍為承旨。

translations.literal: Runfu remained Chief Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Runfu retained his post as Chief Academician after all.

sentences.zh: 周穜乞以王安石配享神宗廟，雍言：「安石持國政，不能上副屬任，非先帝神明，遠而弗用，則其所敗壞，可勝言哉！

translations.literal: Zhou Cong requested that Wang Anshi be granted companion sacrifice in Emperor Shenzong's temple; Yong said: "Anshi held state power and could not fulfill the entrustment from above; had not the late emperor with divine wisdom kept him at a distance and not employed him, the ruin he would have wrought—is it possible to state it all?
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Cong petitioned to have Wang Anshi enshrined as a companion sacrifice in Emperor Shenzong's temple, Zheng Yong objected: "Anshi held the reins of government yet failed to fulfill the trust placed in him. Had the late emperor not possessed the wisdom to keep him at arm's length, the destruction he would have wrought—could words even encompass it?

sentences.zh: 今穜以小臣輒肆橫議，願正其罪。」

translations.literal: Now Zhong, a petty official, presumptuously indulges in reckless talk—I pray his crime be corrected."
translations.idiomatic: That this minor official should now brazenly advance such reckless opinion—I ask that he be duly punished."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The court] assented.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 使契丹還，徙右諫議大夫，言：「朝廷重內輕外，選用牧伯，罕輟從班，以閥閱輕淺者充員，不復為來日慮。

translations.literal: Returning from an embassy to the Khitans, he was transferred to Right Remonstrance Censor and said: "The court values inner [posts] and undervalues outer [posts]; in selecting prefects, it rarely draws from the senior ranks, filling posts with those of slight family pedigree, no longer considering future days.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from an embassy to the Khitan, he was appointed Right Remonstrance Censor and memorialized: "The court esteems capital posts and undervalues provincial service. When appointing prefects, it seldom releases officials from the senior inner ranks, filling vacancies instead with men of shallow pedigree—with no thought for the future.

sentences.zh: 願自今稍積資望，以慚試之。」

translations.literal: I hope from now on to gradually accumulate qualifications and standing, and test them [in outer posts]."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that from now on qualifications and standing be accumulated over time, and that such men be given provincial posts as a proving ground."

sentences.zh: 吳中大飢，方議振恤，以民習欺誕，敕本部料檢，家至戶到。

translations.literal: In Wu there was great famine; they were just discussing relief; because the people were accustomed to fraud, the ministry was ordered to inspect household by household.
translations.idiomatic: When a severe famine struck Wu, and relief was under discussion, the court ordered a house-to-house inspection—on the grounds that the populace was prone to deception.

sentences.zh: 雍言：「此令一布，吏專料民而不救災，民皆死於飢。

translations.literal: Yong said: "Once this order is promulgated, officials will devote themselves only to inspecting the people and not relieve the disaster—the people will all die of famine.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yong warned: "Once this order is issued, officials will devote themselves entirely to inspection rather than to relief—and the people will starve to death.

sentences.zh: 今富有四海，奈何謹圭撮之濫，而輕比屋之死乎？」

translations.literal: Now we possess the four seas in wealth—how can we be strict about petty fraud and lightly treat deaths house by house?"
translations.idiomatic: The empire possesses boundless wealth—how can we fuss over petty fraud while treating whole households dying of hunger as a matter of little consequence?"

sentences.zh: 哲宗悟，追止之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong understood and recalled and halted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhezong saw the point and revoked the order.

sentences.zh: 侍御史賈易沽激自喜，中丞趙彥若懦不自立，雍並論之，遂罷易，左轉彥若，以雍為中丞。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Jia Yi was pretentious and self-satisfied; Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhao Yanruo was timid and could not stand firm; Yong criticized both; Jia Yi was dismissed, Yanruo was transferred to the left, and Yong was made Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Jia Yi was vain and self-aggrandizing; Censor-in-Chief Zhao Yanruo was timid and spineless. Zheng condemned them both. Jia Yi was dismissed, Zhao Yanruo was demoted, and Zheng Yong was appointed Censor-in-Chief in his place.

sentences.zh: 雍辭曰：「中丞以臣言去而身承其乏，非所以厚風俗也。」

translations.literal: Yong declined, saying: "The censor-in-chief left because of my words, yet I personally undertake his vacant post—this is not how to enrich custom."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yong declined the appointment, saying, "The censor-in-chief was removed because of my memorial—yet I would personally succeed to his vacant post. That is no way to uphold public morals."

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: [The request] was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: His resignation was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 時二府禁謁加嚴，雍嘆曰：「旁招俊乂，列於庶位，宅百揆職也。

translations.literal: At the time the two councils had tightened restrictions on visits; Yong sighed, saying: "Broadly recruiting the talented and appointing them to various posts—this is the duty of the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At the time both councils had tightened restrictions on callers. Zheng Yong sighed and said, "It is the chief ministers' duty to seek out the worthy and place them in office throughout the government.

sentences.zh: 彼有足不及公卿之門者，猶當物色致之，奈何設禁若是！

translations.literal: Those whose feet cannot reach the doors of dukes and ministers—even they should be sought out and brought in—why set restrictions like this!
translations.idiomatic: Even men whose means do not allow them to visit the halls of the great should still be sought out and brought forward—why impose restrictions such as these?

sentences.zh: 且二府皆天子所改容而體貌之者，乃復防閒其私如此乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover, the two councils are those whom the Son of Heaven treats with changed countenance and dignified bearing—yet they again guard against private visits like this?"
translations.idiomatic: And the two councils are the very offices before which the Son of Heaven shows special deference—must they really be walled off from private contact to this degree?"

sentences.zh: 於是援賈誼廉恥節行之說以諫，詔弛其禁。

translations.literal: Thereupon he cited Jia Yi's discourse on integrity, shame, and constancy in remonstrance; an edict relaxed the restriction.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon memorialized, invoking Jia Yi's teachings on integrity and shame—and an edict relaxed the restrictions.

sentences.zh: 刑部讞囚，宰執論殺之，有司以為可生，不奉詔，得罪。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice reviewed a prisoner; the chief ministers argued for execution; the relevant office considered him savable and did not obey the edict, incurring punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Justice reviewed a capital case, the chief ministers argued for execution, but the officials responsible judged the prisoner deserving of mercy and refused to carry out the order—whereupon they were punished.

sentences.zh: 雍言：「是固可罪，然究其用心，在於廣好生之德耳，若遽以為罪，臣恐鄰於嗜殺。

translations.literal: Yong said: "This is indeed punishable, yet examining their intent, it lay in extending the virtue of cherishing life—if they are hastily punished, I fear it borders on delight in killing.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yong argued, "They are indeed at fault—but their intent was to extend the virtue of sparing life. To punish them abruptly, I fear, would border on a love of killing.

sentences.zh: 今使有司欲殺而朝廷生之，猶恐仁恩德意不白於天下，而況反是者哉！」

translations.literal: Now if officials wish to kill and the court spares, we still fear benevolent grace and virtue are not made clear to the realm—how much more when it is the reverse!"
translations.idiomatic: When officials wish to execute but the court chooses clemency, we still worry that the emperor's merciful intent may not reach the people—how much worse when officials choose mercy and the court punishes them for it!"

sentences.zh: 哲宗嘉納，囚遂得生。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong commendably accepted; the prisoner was thereby spared.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhezong approved the argument, and the prisoner was spared.

sentences.zh: 初，邢恕以書抵宰相劉摯，摯答之，有『自愛以俟休復』之語，排岸司茹東濟錄書示雍與殿中侍御史楊畏，雍、畏釋其語曰：「『俟休復』者，俟他日太后復辟也。」

translations.literal: Initially, Xing Shu sent a letter to Chief Councilor Liu Zhe; Zhe replied with the phrase 'take care of yourself and await restoration.' Ru Dongji of the river patrol office copied the letter and showed it to Yong and Palace Censor Yang Wei; Yong and Wei interpreted the words: "'Await restoration' means await the day when the Empress Dowager restores her rule."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xing Shu had written to Chief Councilor Liu Zhe, who replied with the phrase, "Take care of yourself and await restoration." Ru Dongji of the river patrol office copied the letter and showed it to Zheng Yong and Palace Censor Yang Wei. Yong and Wei interpreted the phrase: "'Await restoration' means to await the day when the Empress Dowager resumes the regency."

sentences.zh: 遂並以此事論摯威福自恣，乞罷之以收主柄。

translations.literal: Thereupon together they used this matter to argue that Zhe wielded power wantonly, requesting his dismissal to recover the sovereign's authority.
translations.idiomatic: Together they used this to accuse Liu Zhe of arrogating power, petitioning for his removal so that imperial authority might be restored.

sentences.zh: 又論王嚴叟、朱光庭、梁燾等三十人皆為摯黨，以閉其援。

translations.literal: They further argued that Wang Yansou, Zhu Guangting, Liang Dao, and thirty others were all Zhe's faction, to cut off his support.
translations.idiomatic: They further denounced Wang Yansou, Zhu Guangting, Liang Dao, and thirty others as members of Liu Zhe's faction, seeking to cut off his support.

sentences.zh: 及摯出知鄆州，光庭方為給事中，繳還摯麻詞，嚴叟、燾力救之，哲宗以先入之言，不納。

translations.literal: When Zhe went out as prefect of Yun Prefecture, Guangting was then Drafting Speaker; he returned Zhe's appointment edict; Yansou and Dao strenuously pleaded for him; Emperor Zhezong, influenced by prior words, did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhe was sent out as prefect of Yun, Zhu Guangting, then Drafting Speaker, returned Liu's appointment edict unsigned. Yansou and Liang Dao pressed hard for his reinstatement, but Emperor Zhezong, influenced by earlier accusations, refused.

sentences.zh: 雍之攻摯，人以為附左相呂大防也。

translations.literal: Yong's attack on Zhe—people thought he was aligning with Left Chief Councilor Lü Dafang.
translations.idiomatic: Many believed Zheng Yong's attack on Liu Zhe was done to curry favor with Left Chief Councilor Lü Dafang.

sentences.zh: 又有請暴摯陰事者，雍曰：「吾為國擊宰相，非仇摯也。

translations.literal: There were also those who asked to expose Zhe's hidden affairs; Yong said: "I attack the chief councilor for the state, not out of enmity toward Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: When others urged him to expose Liu Zhe's private scandals, Zheng Yong replied, "I am moving against a chief councilor for the good of the state—not out of personal enmity toward Liu Zhe.

sentences.zh: 彼之陰事，何有於國哉？」

translations.literal: What have his hidden affairs to do with the state?"
translations.idiomatic: What do his private failings have to do with the interests of the realm?"

sentences.zh: 置不以聞。

translations.literal: He set the matter aside and did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored the suggestion and made no report.

sentences.zh: 拜尚書右丞，改左丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, then changed to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Vice Grand Councilor, then transferred to Left Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 雍在政地，哲宗稱其事上有禮。

translations.literal: Yong was in the governing circle; Emperor Zhezong praised that his service to superiors had propriety.
translations.idiomatic: While Zheng Yong held high office, Emperor Zhezong commended his respectful and proper conduct toward his superiors.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，治元祐眾臣，雍頓首自列，哲宗明其亡他心，諭使勿去。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng, when the Yuanyou officials were prosecuted, Yong bowed his head and listed himself; Emperor Zhezong understood he had no other intent and instructed him not to leave.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shaosheng era, when Yuanyou officials came under investigation, Zheng Yong prostrated himself and voluntarily included himself among them. Emperor Zhezong understood he harbored no ulterior motive and urged him to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 周秩乘隙抵之，謂雍初為侍從時，因徐王私於權臣以進。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhi seized the opportunity to denounce him, saying that when Yong was first in the attendant ranks, he had advanced through private dealings with powerful ministers via Prince Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhi seized the moment to attack him, alleging that in his early days as an imperial attendant, Zheng Yong had advanced through secret dealings with Prince Xu and powerful ministers at court.

sentences.zh: 哲宗怒曰：「此是何言也！

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong angrily said: "What sort of talk is this!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhezong said in anger, "What kind of accusation is this!

sentences.zh: 使徐王聞之，豈能自安？」

translations.literal: If Prince Xu heard it, how could he be at ease?"
translations.idiomatic: If Prince Xu were to hear such a thing, how could he rest easy?"

sentences.zh: 黜秩知廣德軍，敕銀台毋受雍辭去奏章，東府吏毋聽雍妻子輒出，且令學士錢勰善為留詔。

translations.literal: He demoted Zhou Zhi to serve as prefect of the Guangde Army command, ordered the Silver Terrace not to accept Zheng Yong's memorials of resignation, the Eastern Chancellery clerks not to allow Zheng Yong's wife and children to leave at will, and commanded Academician Qian Su to draft a retention edict with care.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhou Zhi away to serve as prefect of Guangde Army, ordered the Silver Terrace to refuse any memorial in which Zheng Yong tried to resign, forbade the Eastern Chancellery staff to let Zheng Yong's wife and children leave on their own, and told Academician Qian Su to prepare a carefully worded edict to keep him in office.

sentences.zh: 二年，始以資政殿學士知陳州，徙北京留守。

translations.literal: In the second year, only then was he appointed Privy Council academician and prefect of Chenzhou, then transferred to garrison commissioner of Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Zheng Yong was at last made a Privy Council academician and prefect of Chenzhou, and then transferred to serve as garrison commissioner of Beijing.

sentences.zh: 初，章惇以白帖貶謫元祐臣僚，安燾爭論不已，哲宗疑之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Dun had used white notes to demote and banish the Yuanyou officials; An Tuo argued against it without cease, and Zhezong grew doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhang Dun had demoted and exiled Yuanyou officials by means of informal white notes. An Tuo kept arguing against the practice, and Zhezong began to have doubts.

sentences.zh: 雍欲為自安計，謂惇曰：「熙寧初，王安石作相，常用白帖行事。」

translations.literal: Zheng Yong, seeking a plan to secure himself, said to Dun: "At the beginning of the Xining era, when Wang Anshi served as chief minister, he often conducted affairs by white notes."
translations.idiomatic: Looking for a way to protect himself, Zheng Yong told Dun, "In the early Xining years, when Wang Anshi was chief minister, he often governed by informal white notes."

sentences.zh: 惇大喜，取其案牘懷之，以白哲宗，遂其奸。

translations.literal: Dun was greatly pleased, took the case documents and hid them in his robe, reported this to Zhezong, and thus carried out his scheme.
translations.idiomatic: Dun was delighted, tucked the case documents into his robe, reported the matter to Zhezong, and thus got his way.

sentences.zh: 雍雖以此結惇，然卒罷政，坐元祐黨，奪職知鄭州。

translations.literal: Although Zheng Yong thereby won Dun over, in the end he was removed from power, convicted as a Yuanyou partisan, stripped of rank, and made prefect of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yong did win Dun's favor by this, but he was still driven from office in the end, condemned as a Yuanyou partisan, stripped of his post, and sent to govern Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 數日，改成都府。

translations.literal: After several days, he was reassigned to Chengdu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later he was reassigned to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 元符元年，提舉崇福宮，歸，未至而卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfu, he was appointed overseer of Chongfu Palace; on his way home he died before arriving, at the age of sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfu 1 he was appointed overseer of Chongfu Palace. He set out for home but died on the road before he arrived, aged sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 政和中，復資政殿學士。

translations.literal: In the Zhenghe era, his Privy Council academician rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenghe reign his title of Privy Council academician was posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 孫永，字曼叔，世為趙人，徙長社。

translations.literal: Sun Yong, courtesy name Manshu, was for generations a man of Zhao and moved to Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yong, whose courtesy name was Manshu, came from a Zhao family that had moved to Changshe.

sentences.zh: 年十歲孤，祖給事中沖，列為子行，蔭將作監主簿，肄業西學，群試常第一。

translations.literal: Orphaned at ten, his grandfather, Supervising Secretary Chong, entered him in the register as a son; by inherited privilege he became a registrar of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, studied at the Western Academy, and in group examinations often ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at ten. His grandfather, Supervising Secretary Chong, had him entered in the family register as a son. By inherited privilege he became a registrar in the Directorate of Palace Buildings, pursued his studies at the Western Academy, and repeatedly placed first in the group examinations.

sentences.zh: 沖戒之曰：「洛陽英雋所萃，汝年少，不宜多上人。」

translations.literal: Chong admonished him, saying: "Luoyang gathers the finest talent of the realm; you are still young and should not too often outrank your elders."
translations.idiomatic: Chong warned him, "Luoyang draws the brightest men in the empire. You are still young; you should not so often place above your seniors."

sentences.zh: 自是不覆試。

translations.literal: From then on he no longer repeated the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: After that he stopped sitting for the examinations again.

sentences.zh: 沖卒，喪除，復列為孫，換試銜，擢進士第，調襄城尉、宜城令，至太常博士。

translations.literal: When Chong died and the mourning was over, he was again entered as a grandson, exchanged his rank for examination standing, passed the jinshi examination, and was appointed magistrate of Xiangcheng, magistrate of Yicheng, and eventually reached the post of Erudite of the Grand Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After Chong's death and the period of mourning, he was entered once more as a grandson, converted his privilege into examination standing, passed the jinshi examination, and served successively as magistrate of Xiangcheng and Yicheng before rising to Erudite of the Grand Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞賈黯薦為御史，以母老不就。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Jia An recommended him for the censorate, but because his mother was old he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Jia An recommended him for appointment as a censor, but he declined because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 韓琦讀其詩，嘆譽之，引為諸王府侍讀。

translations.literal: Han Qi read his poetry, sighed in praise, and brought him in as lecturer to the princes' household.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi read his poems, admired them greatly, and had him appointed lecturer in the princes' household.

sentences.zh: 神宗為潁王，出新錄《韓非子》畀宮僚讎定，永曰：「非險薄刻核，其書背《六經》之旨，願毋留意。」

translations.literal: When Shenzong was Prince of Ying, he issued a newly collated Han Feizi for the palace staff to revise; Yong said: "Han Fei was treacherous, harsh, and narrow; his book goes against the intent of the Six Classics. I hope Your Highness will not give it attention."
translations.idiomatic: When the future Shenzong was Prince of Ying, he circulated a newly edited Han Feizi for the palace staff to review. Yong said, "Han Fei was treacherous, harsh, and unyielding, and his book runs counter to the Six Classics. I hope Your Highness will pay it no mind."

sentences.zh: 王曰：「廣藏書之數耳，非所好也。」

translations.literal: The prince said: "It is only to increase the number of books in the collection, not something I favor."
translations.idiomatic: The prince replied, "I only mean to enlarge the library. It is not a book I care for."

sentences.zh: 及為皇太子，進舍人；

translations.literal: When he became crown prince, Yong was promoted to Gentleman Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: When he became crown prince, Yong was promoted to Gentleman Attendant.

sentences.zh: 即位，擢天章閣待制，安撫陝西。

translations.literal: when he took the throne, Yong was raised to Tiantangge Attendant Gentleman and pacification commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince ascended the throne, Yong was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Tiantang Pavilion and made pacification commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 民景詢外叛，詔捕送其孥，勿以赦原。

translations.literal: The commoner Jing Xun defected abroad; an edict ordered that his wife and children be seized and sent in, and that no amnesty should cover them.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner named Jing Xun defected beyond the border. The court ordered his wife and children seized and sent in, and decreed that no amnesty should apply to those implicated with him.

sentences.zh: 永言：「陛下新御極，曠澤流行，惡逆者猶得虧除。

translations.literal: Yong said: "Your Majesty has newly ascended the throne; broad clemency is flowing forth, and even the wicked and rebellious may receive mitigation.
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "Your Majesty has only just taken the throne. A wide clemency is being proclaimed, and even the wicked and rebellious may have their penalties reduced.

sentences.zh: 今緣坐者弗宥，非所以示信也。」

translations.literal: Now to deny pardon to those implicated by association is not the way to show good faith."
translations.idiomatic: To withhold pardon from those punished only by association is not the way to show the people that the throne keeps its word."

sentences.zh: 歷河北、陝西都轉運使。

translations.literal: He served successively as transport commissioner of Hebei and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as transport commissioner for Hebei and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 時邊用不足，以解鹽、市馬別為一司，外台不得與。

translations.literal: At the time frontier expenses were insufficient; salt vouchers and horse procurement were made into a separate office, and the outer commissions were not allowed to interfere.
translations.idiomatic: At that time frontier funds were short, so salt vouchers and horse procurement were placed in a separate agency beyond the reach of the regional transport commissions.

sentences.zh: 永奏曰：「鹽、馬，國之大計，使主者專其柄，既無以統隸，苟為非法，孰從而制之？」

translations.literal: Yong memorialized, saying: "Salt and horses are great matters of state. If those in charge hold exclusive authority, with no higher body to command them, and they act unlawfully, who will restrain them?"
translations.idiomatic: Yong memorialized, "Salt and horses are vital to the state. If the officials in charge hold sole authority with no superior to command them, and they turn to illegal practices, who will be able to check them?"

sentences.zh: 加龍圖閣直學士、知秦州。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title of Dragon Diagram Hall Direct Academician and made prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 王韶以布衣入幕府，建取熙河策，永折之曰：「邊陲方安靜，無故騷動，恐變生不測。」

translations.literal: Wang Shao entered the staff as a commoner and proposed a strategy to seize the Xihe region; Yong refuted him, saying: "The frontier is just now quiet; to stir trouble without cause may bring unforeseen change."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao joined the staff as a commoner and urged a campaign to take the Xihe region. Yong objected: "The borderlands have only just settled down. To provoke unrest without cause may bring disaster we cannot foresee."

sentences.zh: 會新築劉家堡失利，眾請戮偏裨以塞責。

translations.literal: It happened that the newly built Liujia Fort suffered defeat; the crowd asked that junior officers be executed to answer for it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the newly built Liujia Fort was lost in battle, and many demanded that junior officers be executed to satisfy blame.

sentences.zh: 永曰：「居敵必爭之地，軍孤援絕，兵法所謂不得而守者也。

translations.literal: Yong said: "They held ground the enemy was bound to contest; the army was isolated and reinforcements cut off—what the art of war calls a position that cannot be defended.
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "They held ground the enemy was sure to fight for, with a lone force and no relief. That is what the military classics call a place that cannot be held.

sentences.zh: 尤人以自免，於我安乎？」

translations.literal: To blame others in order to save oneself—how can that sit well with us?"
translations.idiomatic: To shift blame onto others to save ourselves—how can we live with that?"

sentences.zh: 竟用是降天章閣待制、知和州，以詳定編敕知審官東院召還，神守問：「青苗、助役之法，於民便否？」

translations.literal: In the end, because of this he was demoted to Tiantangge Attendant Gentleman and prefect of Hezhou; then, as compiler of statutes and director of the Eastern Bureau for Review of Appointments, he was recalled. Shenzong asked: "Are the Green Sprouts and corvee substitution laws convenient for the people?"
translations.idiomatic: Because of this he was eventually demoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Tiantang Pavilion and prefect of Hezhou. Later, while serving as compiler of statutes and director of the Eastern Bureau for Review of Appointments, he was recalled to court. Shenzong asked, "Do the Green Sprouts and corvee substitution laws benefit the people?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「法誠善，然強民出息輸錢代徭，不能無重斂之患。

translations.literal: He replied: "The laws are indeed good, yet when the people are forced to pay interest and money in place of corvee labor, one cannot be free of the harm of heavy exaction.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The laws are sound in principle, but when common people are forced to pay interest and cash in lieu of corvee, the burden of heavy levies cannot be avoided.

sentences.zh: 若用以資經費，非臣所知也。」

translations.literal: If they are used to supply state expenses, that is not something this subject understands."
translations.idiomatic: Whether they should be used to finance state expenditure is beyond what I can judge."

sentences.zh: 時倉法峻密，庾吏受百錢，則黥為卒，府史亦如之。

translations.literal: At the time the granary law was severe and exacting: if a granary clerk accepted as little as a hundred cash, he was tattooed and made a soldier, and clerks in prefectural offices were treated the same.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the granary regulations were harsh. If a granary clerk took so little as a hundred cash, he was tattooed and enrolled as a soldier; prefectural clerks were subject to the same rule.

sentences.zh: 神宗又問：「此法既下，吏尚為奸乎？」

translations.literal: Shenzong again asked: "Since this law was issued, do clerks still commit fraud?"
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong asked again, "Since this law was promulgated, do clerks still commit fraud?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「強盜罪死，犯者猶眾，況配隸邪？

translations.literal: He replied: "Robbery is punishable by death, yet offenders are still numerous; how much more so when the penalty is forced labor?
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Highway robbery carries the death penalty, yet offenders remain numerous. How much more so when the punishment is only assignment to corvee?

sentences.zh: 使人畏法而不革心，雖在府史，臣亦不敢必其無犯也。」

translations.literal: If men fear the law but do not reform their hearts, then even among prefectural clerks I dare not guarantee that none will offend."
translations.idiomatic: If people fear punishment but do not change within, then even among prefectural clerks I would not dare swear that none will offend."

sentences.zh: 議復肉刑，事下永。

translations.literal: When the court debated restoring corporal punishment, the matter was referred to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated restoring corporal mutilation as punishment, the matter was sent down to Yong.

sentences.zh: 永奏曰：「刻人肌膚，深害仁政，漢文帝所不忍，陛下忍之乎？」

translations.literal: Yong memorialized, saying: "To carve human flesh deeply harms humane government; Emperor Wen of Han could not bear it—can Your Majesty bear it?"
translations.idiomatic: Yong memorialized, "To cut and mutilate human flesh does grave injury to humane rule. Emperor Wen of Han could not bear such a thing. Can Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「事固未決，待卿始定耳。」

translations.literal: Shenzong said: "The matter is indeed undecided; I was waiting for you to settle it."
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong said, "The matter is still unsettled. I was waiting for you to decide it."

sentences.zh: 不果行。

translations.literal: In the end it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 復學士，知瀛州。

translations.literal: He was restored to academician and made prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored to academician and appointed prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 河決，於貝、瀛、冀尤甚，民租以災免者，州縣懼常平法，征催如故。

translations.literal: The Yellow River broke its banks; Bei, Ying, and Ji suffered especially, and though rent was remitted on account of the disaster, the prefectures and counties, fearing the Ever-Normal Granary regulations, collected and pressed payment as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River burst its dikes. Bei, Ying, and Ji were hit hardest. Although land tax had been remitted because of the disaster, local officials, afraid of the Ever-Normal Granary rules, kept collecting and pressing for payment as before.

sentences.zh: 永連章論止，神宗從之，仍命發廩粟以振。

translations.literal: Yong submitted successive memorials urging that this stop; Shenzong agreed and also ordered granary grain issued for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Yong submitted repeated memorials demanding that the collections cease. Shenzong agreed and also ordered grain from the state granaries distributed in relief.

sentences.zh: 白溝巡檢趙用以遼人漁界河，擅引兵北度，盪其族帳，遼持此兆釁，數暴邊上，神宗遣使問故，永請正用罪以謝，未報，遼屯兵連營互四十里，永好諭之曰：「疆吏冒禁，已置之獄矣，今何為者？」

translations.literal: Baimao patrol inspector Zhao Yong, because Liao people were fishing in the border river, on his own authority led troops north across the river and raided their camps and tents; the Liao seized on this as a portent of conflict and repeatedly raided the frontier. Shenzong sent an envoy to ask the reason; Yong requested that Zhao Yong be punished according to law as an apology. Before a reply came, the Liao massed troops in linked camps for forty li. Yong spoke to them persuasively, saying: "The frontier official violated the prohibition and has already been placed in prison. What are you doing now?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yong, patrol inspector at Baimao, saw Liao fishermen working the border river and on his own authority led troops north across the river to raid their camps. The Liao took this as a pretext for hostilities and repeatedly struck the frontier. Shenzong sent an envoy to inquire into the cause. Yong asked that Zhao Yong be punished according to law as an apology to Liao. Before any answer arrived, Liao troops camped in linked encampments stretching forty li. Yong reasoned with them gently: "The frontier official who broke the prohibition is already in prison. What is the purpose of this?"

sentences.zh: 敵意解，但求醪Я犒師而旋。

translations.literal: The enemy's intent eased; they asked only for wine and grain to reward the troops and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao relented. They asked only for wine and provisions to reward their troops, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 進樞密直學士、知開封府。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Privy Council Direct Academician and made prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Direct Academician of the Privy Council and appointed prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 呂嘉問言，吏欲使都人列肆輸錢以免直。

translations.literal: Lü Jiawen reported that officials wished to have shopkeepers in the capital pay money in lieu of corvee labor.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Jiawen reported that officials wanted shopkeepers throughout the capital to pay cash in place of corvee service.

sentences.zh: 下府詢究，曹椽以為便。

translations.literal: The matter was sent to the prefectural office for inquiry; the bureau clerks thought it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was referred to the prefectural office for investigation, and the bureau clerks judged it expedient.

sentences.zh: 永占書紙尾，不暇省。

translations.literal: Yong casually signed at the end of the document without time to examine it.
translations.idiomatic: Yong initialed the bottom of the document without taking time to read it through.

sentences.zh: 既乃行市易抵當法，貸民錢而為之期，有不能償而死者。

translations.literal: Only afterward was the market trade and pawn law put into effect, lending the people's money on fixed terms; some who could not repay died.
translations.idiomatic: Only afterward was the market trade and pawn law implemented, lending money to common people on fixed terms. Some who could not repay died under the burden.

sentences.zh: 神宗頗知之，嘉問妄變其名以罔聽。

translations.literal: Shenzong knew something of this; Jiawen falsely changed its name to deceive the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong had some knowledge of this, but Jiawen changed the name of the scheme to mislead the throne.

sentences.zh: 神宗慮立法未盡，詔永及韓維究實。

translations.literal: Shenzong, fearing the legislation was not yet complete, ordered Yong and Han Wei to investigate the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Concerned that the legislation was still incomplete, Shenzong ordered Yong and Han Wei to investigate the facts.

sentences.zh: 永奏言：「市算下逮錐刀，為人患苦。」

translations.literal: Yong memorialized, saying: "Market levies reach even to knives and awls, to the people's great distress."
translations.idiomatic: Yong memorialized, "Market taxes reach even to knives and awls, causing the people great suffering."

sentences.zh: 御史張琥劾永棄同即異，罷為提舉中太一宮。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Hu impeached Yong for abandoning a shared position once agreement was reached and taking a different one; he was dismissed and made overseer of the Zhongtaiyi Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Hu impeached Yong for agreeing with the policy and then turning against it. Yong was removed and made overseer of the Zhongtaiyi Palace.

sentences.zh: 元豐中，判軍器監。

translations.literal: In the Yuanfeng era he served as vice director of the Directorate of Armaments.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfeng reign he served as vice director of the Directorate of Armaments.

sentences.zh: 有司病皮革不給，嚴隱匿之科，亡賴輩肆情為訐，至婦人冠飾亦不免。

translations.literal: The relevant offices complained that leather supplies were insufficient and imposed strict penalties for concealment; idle scoundrels indulged in malicious accusations, so that even women's headdresses were not spared.
translations.idiomatic: The offices complained of insufficient leather supplies and imposed harsh penalties for concealment. Idle troublemakers filed malicious accusations freely, so that even women's headdresses were not exempt.

sentences.zh: 永請聽人以所藏之善者售於官，得貸其餘，訐訟既息，國用亦濟。

translations.literal: Yong requested that people be allowed to sell the good pieces they had stored to the government and borrow against the rest; malicious lawsuits ceased and state needs were also met.
translations.idiomatic: Yong asked that people be allowed to sell their best stored hides to the government and borrow against the remainder. Malicious lawsuits died down, and state needs were met as well.

sentences.zh: 出知太原，且行，神宗訪以時務，永言：「近者造戎器倍常，外間謂將有事於征討。

translations.literal: Sent out to govern Taiyuan, and about to depart, Shenzong consulted him on current affairs; Yong said: "Recently the manufacture of weapons has doubled the usual rate; outside the court people say there will be a campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When he was sent to govern Taiyuan and was about to leave, Shenzong asked his view of current affairs. Yong said, "Recently weapons production has doubled the usual rate. Outside the palace people believe a campaign is coming.

sentences.zh: 兵非輕用之物，原軫不戢自焚之戒。」

translations.literal: Arms are not a thing to be used lightly; I pray Your Majesty will heed Yuanzhen's warning about failing to restrain oneself and bringing ruin upon oneself."
translations.idiomatic: Arms are not to be used lightly. I beg Your Majesty to take to heart Yuanzhen's warning about failing to restrain oneself and destroying oneself in the end."

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「此備豫不虞，若四方安平，豈有輕動之理？

translations.literal: Shenzong said: "This is preparation against the unexpected; if all four quarters are peaceful, how could there be any thought of rash action?
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong said, "This is precaution against the unforeseen. If the realm is at peace on every side, why would we act rashly?

sentences.zh: 卿言是也。」

translations.literal: What you say is right."
translations.idiomatic: What you say is right."

sentences.zh: 忻、代產鹽，苦惡不堪食，轉運使必欲理之，以盜販闌越之罪罪兵吏。

translations.literal: The salt produced in Xin and Dai was bitter and foul, unfit for food; the transport commissioner insisted on regulating it and punished frontier soldiers and clerks with the crime of smuggling and illegal crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Salt from Xin and Dai was bitter and unfit to eat, yet the transport commissioner insisted on regulating it and punished frontier soldiers and clerks for smuggling and illegal crossing.

sentences.zh: 永言：「鹽，民食也，不可禁；

translations.literal: Yong said: "Salt is the people's food and cannot be forbidden;
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "Salt is the people's food and cannot be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 兵，武備也，不可闕。

translations.literal: soldiers are military preparedness and cannot be neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers are the foundation of defense and cannot be neglected.

sentences.zh: 顧以惡鹽累防兵，非計也。」

translations.literal: Yet to burden frontier troops because of bad salt is no sound plan."
translations.idiomatic: To burden frontier troops over bad salt is no sound policy."

sentences.zh: 詔弛其禁。

translations.literal: An edict relaxed the prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: An edict relaxed the prohibition.

sentences.zh: 永外和內勁，論議常持平，不求詭異。

translations.literal: Yong was outwardly mild and inwardly firm; in debate he usually held the middle ground and did not seek the bizarre or unusual.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly mild and inwardly firm, Yong usually argued from the middle ground and never courted the bizarre.

sentences.zh: 事或悖於理，雖逼以勢，亦不為屈。

translations.literal: When a matter ran against reason, even if pressed by power, he would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: When a matter violated reason, he would not bend even under pressure.

sentences.zh: 未嘗以矯亢形於色辭，與人交，終身無怨仇。

translations.literal: He never showed arrogance in expression or speech; in dealings with others he bore no grudges to the end of his life.
translations.idiomatic: He never wore haughtiness on his face or in his words, and in all his dealings he made no lifelong enemies.

sentences.zh: 范純仁、蘇頌皆稱之為國器。

translations.literal: Fan Chunren and Su Song both called him a vessel of state.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chunren and Su Song both called him material fit to sustain the state.

sentences.zh: 論曰：「宋之衰也，人才尚多。

translations.literal: The commentators say: "In the decline of Song, talent was still abundant.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: "Even in Song's decline, men of talent were still plentiful.

sentences.zh: 梁燾、王岩叟盡忠事上，凡有過舉，知無不言，雖或從或違，而隱然有虎豹在山之勢矣。

translations.literal: Liang Dao and Wang Yansou served the throne with full loyalty; whenever there was a misstep, they spoke without reserve. Though sometimes heeded and sometimes rejected, they still possessed, invisibly, the force of tigers and leopards on the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Dao and Wang Yansou served the throne with complete loyalty. Whenever the court erred, they spoke without reserve. Whether heeded or rejected, they still carried, unseen, the force of tigers and leopards on the mountain.

sentences.zh: 第以新州之舉，於是為過。

translations.literal: Only in the affair of Xinzhou was there fault.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the Xinzhou affair did they go too far.

sentences.zh: 故他日紹聖復以藉口，使元祐眾賢皆罹其禍，由是再變而為宣、政之奸臣，國日危矣。

translations.literal: Thus later, in the Shaosheng era, that was again seized as a pretext, and the worthy men of Yuanyou all suffered disaster; from this the court changed once more into the corrupt ministers of the Xuanhe and Zhenghe reigns, and the state grew daily more perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in the Shaosheng era, that very episode became a pretext again, and the worthy men of Yuanyou were swept into calamity. From that point the court turned once more toward the corrupt ministers of the Xuanhe and Zhenghe reigns, and the state grew more perilous by the day.

sentences.zh: 鄭雍易其所守，肆擊劉摯，波及者三十人，欲結章惇以取容，然而終亦不免。

translations.literal: Zheng Yong changed what he had upheld, recklessly attacked Liu Zhi, and implicated thirty men, seeking to win Zhang Dun's favor—yet in the end he could not escape ruin himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yong abandoned his former principles, attacked Liu Zhi without restraint, and implicated thirty men, hoping to curry favor with Zhang Dun—yet in the end he could not save himself.

sentences.zh: 小人反覆，專務自全，竟何益哉？

translations.literal: Petty men are fickle and devote themselves wholly to self-preservation—what good does it do in the end?
translations.idiomatic: Petty men turn with every wind and devote themselves only to self-preservation. What good does it do them in the end?

sentences.zh: 孫永之為人，庶得其中焉。

translations.literal: In his conduct, Sun Yong may be said to have held the mean.
translations.idiomatic: In his character, Sun Yong may be said to have kept to the middle way.
